q: אישה בת 83 עם דמנציה מגיעה לבית החולים עם חבורות בגב ובזרוע שאינה יכולה להסביר. לאחר ההערכה הראשונית מתעורר בצוות חשד להתעמרות. לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות לטיפול בנפגעי התעמרות, מתי יש להזמין רופא לבדיקתה?
o: יש להזמין רופא לאחר השלמת שיחה מתועדת עם בני המשפחה
יש להזמין רופא לאחר קבלת הערכת הסיכון מהעובד הסוציאלי
יש להזמין רופא מיד עם התעוררות החשד לפגיעה במטופלת
יש להזמין רופא לאחר בירור פניות קודמות לבתי חולים
explanation:
הצוות מזמין בדיקה רפואית עם הופעת סימנים לפגיעה בזקן. בירור סוציאלי והגנה יכולים להתקיים במקביל. **יש להזמין רופא מיד עם התעוררות החשד לפגיעה במטופלת**.

**א. יש להזמין רופא לאחר השלמת שיחה מתועדת עם בני המשפחה.** שיחה עם המשפחה אינה תנאי לבדיקה.
**ב. יש להזמין רופא לאחר קבלת הערכת הסיכון מהעובד הסוציאלי.** אין להמתין להשלמת הערכת העו״ס כדי לטפל בפגיעה.
**ג. יש להזמין רופא מיד עם התעוררות החשד לפגיעה במטופלת.** בדיקה מוקדמת מאפשרת טיפול ותיעוד ממצאים לפני שייעלמו.
**ד. יש להזמין רופא לאחר בירור פניות קודמות לבתי חולים.** תיקים קודמים יכולים לסייע אך אינם תנאי להזמנת רופא.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל לטיפול בנפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 6, סעיפים 8.1 עד 8.4 ו־8.7.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: גבר בן 76 עם דמנציה multi-infarct, CKD stage 4 (eGFR 24) וסוכרת, מאושפז מבית אבות עם AKI (Cr 4.2, baseline 2.8) והיפרקלמיה (K 6.1). בסקירת התיק עולה כי זו אשפוזו הרביעי תוך חודשיים בגין בעיות דומות. בכל פעם מצבו משתפר עם IV fluids וחוזר ל-baseline. הדיווח מהמתקן הוא שהוא לעיתים קרובות מסרב לתרופות ולארוחות. היום הוא מבולבל יותר מה-baseline שלו (CAM חיובי). איזה גורם מצביע ביותר על הזנחה שיטתית?
o: אשפוזים חוזרים בגין dehydration שניתן היה למנוע
סירוב המטופל לטיפול עקב דמנציה
AKI על רקע CKD כרוני בחולה סוכרת
התפתחות delirium עם הפרעות מטבוליות
explanation:
הזנחה שיטתית נשקלת כשיש דפוס חוזר של חסרים הניתנים למניעה אצל אדם תלוי. מחלה חריפה יחידה היא ממצא פחות ספציפי. **אשפוזים חוזרים בגין dehydration שניתן היה למנוע**.

**א. אשפוזים חוזרים בגין dehydration שניתן היה למנוע.** התייבשויות חוזרות בתנאי טיפול בלתי מספק מחייבות בירור של שתייה, השגחה ועזרה.
**ב. סירוב המטופל לטיפול עקב דמנציה.** יש לברר את הסיבה לסירוב ואי אפשר להסיק ממנו לבדו הזנחה.
**ג. AKI על רקע CKD כרוני בחולה סוכרת.** פגיעה כלייתית חדה יכולה לנבוע מסיבות רפואיות רבות.
**ד. התפתחות delirium עם הפרעות מטבוליות.** דליריום מעיד על מחלה חריפה ואינו מוכיח את הגורם החברתי.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 4, 6 ונספח 1 עמ׳ 2.

q: אלמנה בת 81 עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה (MCI) (MoCA 22) ודגנרציה מקולרית מספרת לרופא המשפחה שלה שאחיינה, שהפך לאחרונה למיופה הכוח שלה, לוקח אותה לבנק לעתים קרובות. היא לא בטוחה מדוע, אך מבחינה שהיתרות בחשבון החיסכון שלה הולכות ויורדות. היא תלויה בו לקניות (Lawton-Brody IADL 5/8) ונראית מפוחדת כשמדברים על כך. התרופות שלה כוללות donepezil 10mg וויטמינים יומיים. איזה סוג של התעמרות בזקנים מתרחש כאן בסבירות הגבוהה ביותר?
o: התעמרות פיזית עם הפחדה
התעמרות נפשית עם איומים
ניצול כלכלי
הזנחה על ידי מטפל
explanation:
ניצול כלכלי כולל שימוש בנכסיו של אדם ללא רשותו או באופן המנצל תלות וחוסר יכולת להגן עליהם. **ניצול כלכלי**.

**א. התעמרות פיזית עם הפחדה.** לא תוארה פגיעה בכוח גופני.
**ב. התעמרות נפשית עם איומים.** איום יכול להתלוות למעשה, אך ליבת המקרה היא שימוש בנכסים.
**ג. ניצול כלכלי.** הדרך שבה נעשה שימוש בכסף היא הסימן המכוון.
**ד. הזנחה על ידי מטפל.** הזנחה מתארת חסך במענה לצרכיו הבסיסיים.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 4, סעיפים 5.8 עד 5.11.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: אישה בת 85 התלויה בבנה לצרכיה הבסיסיים ואינה מסוגלת להגן על עצמה מספרת בחדר המיון שהוא נועל אותה בחדר ומונע ממנה טיפול. לאחר ייצוב מצבה הרפואי קיים חשד סביר להתעמרות מצד המטפל. איזו פעולה נדרשת כעת לפי הנוהל?
o: לערב עובד סוציאלי, להגן ולדווח לפקיד סעד או למשטרה
לתאם פגישת משפחה בקהילה כדי לבנות תכנית השגחה והמשך טיפול
להעביר בירור למרפאה הגריאטרית כדי להעריך תפקוד ותמיכה בבית
לתאם מעקב סיעודי בבית כדי להעריך את ניהול התרופות בידי הבן
explanation:
חשד סביר להתעמרות בידי מטפל מחייב פעולה בזמן המפגש: טיפול, הגנה, הערכה סוציאלית ותיעוד, לצד הדיווח הנדרש. **לערב עובד סוציאלי, להגן ולדווח לפקיד סעד או למשטרה**.

**א. לערב עובד סוציאלי, להגן ולדווח לפקיד סעד או למשטרה.** מעורבות העו״ס והפנייה לגורם המוסמך נותנות מענה לסיכון המיידי.
**ב. לתאם פגישת משפחה בקהילה כדי לבנות תכנית השגחה והמשך טיפול.** פגישה עתידית אינה מחליפה דיווח והגנה כעת.
**ג. להעביר בירור למרפאה הגריאטרית כדי להעריך תפקוד ותמיכה בבית.** בירור גריאטרי מתוכנן אינו פותר סכנה בהווה.
**ד. לתאם מעקב סיעודי בבית כדי להעריך את ניהול התרופות בידי הבן.** מעקב תרופתי בבית אינו בירור מלא של פגיעה.

אסמכתא · נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 2, 6, סעיפים 1.2, 8–10.
ref: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF pp.2, 6, sections 1.2, 8–10
label: Source: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF pp.2, 6, sections 1.2, 8–10

q: בביקור בית נמצא שמטפל אינו מספק לזקן מזון ותרופות הנחוצים לצרכיו הבסיסיים. לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות, איזו קטגוריה מתארת ישירות את המעשה?
o: התעמרות כלכלית באמצעות שימוש בכספו בלי הסכמה
הזנחה המתבטאת בכשל במילוי צרכיו הבסיסיים
התעמרות פיזית באמצעות שימוש בכוח נגד גופו
התעמרות נפשית באמצעות פגיעה ברגשותיו וביזויו
explanation:
השארת אדם תלוי ללא מענה לצורכי מחיה וטיפול בסיסיים מתאימה להזנחה. **הזנחה המתבטאת בכשל במילוי צרכיו הבסיסיים**.

**א. התעמרות כלכלית באמצעות שימוש בכספו בלי הסכמה.** ניצול כספי כולל שימוש בנכסים ללא הרשאה.
**ב. הזנחה המתבטאת בכשל במילוי צרכיו הבסיסיים.** הפגיעה הישירה כאן היא חסך בצרכים שהתלות מונעת מהאדם למלא.
**ג. התעמרות פיזית באמצעות שימוש בכוח נגד גופו.** לא תוארה הפעלת כוח על גופו.
**ד. התעמרות נפשית באמצעות פגיעה ברגשותיו וביזויו.** פגיעה רגשית מכוונת היא סוג אחר של התעמרות.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 4.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: במטופלת מבית אבות נמצאו כיבי לחץ וירידה במשקל, ונוצר חשד להזנחה. מהי הפעולה הנדרשת לפי נוהל הטיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות?
o: להמתין להכרעה אם הממצאים נובעים ממחלה לפני הזמנת רופא
לבקש מהמלווים לתאר את המצב בנוכחות המטופלת במהלך הבדיקה
להזמין רופא לבדיקה מיידית ולהזמין את העובד הסוציאלי
להמשיך מעקב סיעודי ולדחות את הבדיקה למועד הביקור השגרתי
explanation:
**יש להזמין רופא לבדיקה מיידית ולערב עובד סוציאלי.** פצעי לחץ וירידה במשקל דורשים טיפול ובירור משולב של מחלה, תזונה, טיפול יומיומי ובטיחות.

**א. המתנה להכרעה בסיבה.** הערכה רפואית מיידית נדרשת גם כאשר האטיולוגיה עדיין אינה ידועה.
**ב. בירור משותף בנוכחות מלווים.** יש לאפשר למטופלת לדבר בפרטיות.
**ג. רופא ועובד סוציאלי.** משלבים תיעוד קליני, הערכת סיכון ותוכנית הגנה ודיווח כשמתקיימים התנאים.
**ד. מעקב שגרתי בלבד.** עלול להותיר פגיעה או הזנחה פעילה ללא טיפול.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, סעיפים 8.1–8.2.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: גבר בן 78 עם סוכרת, neuropathy פריפרית, ודמנציה קלה מסוג אלצהיימר (MMSE 20) מגיע לטיפול דחוף עקב זיהום ברגל. אשתו, המטפלת העיקרית שלו, הביאה אותו לאחר שעוזרת הבית הביעה דאגה. בבדיקה: אצבע רגל נקרוטית עם ריח רע ודלף מוגלתי, ומספר אזורים נוספים של פירוק רקמות בשתי הרגליים. האישה אומרת: 'אני בודקת את הרגליים שלו כל יום כמו שאמרו לי.' ה-HbA1c של המטופל הוא 11.8%. איזה היבט מצביע בצורה החזקה ביותר על caregiver neglect?
o: זיהום ברגל אצל מטופל הסובל גם מנוירופתיה סוכרתית
פער בין דיווח המטפלת לממצאים החמורים בבדיקת הרגל
סוכרת שאינה מאוזנת אצל מטופל עם ליקוי קוגניטיבי
זיהוי הבעיה בידי עוזרת הבית ולא בידי האישה
explanation:
**פער בולט בין הדיווח על בדיקה יומית לבין נמק, מוגלה ופצעים מרובים** מעורר חשד להזנחה. מדובר בסימן אזהרה המחייב בירור, לצד טיפול דחוף בזיהום.

**א. זיהום עם נוירופתיה.** זהו סיבוך מוכר של סוכרת גם בטיפול מסור.
**ב. אי־התאמה בין ההסבר לממצאים.** הפער מצדיק תיעוד, שיחה נפרדת ובחינת זמינות הטיפול והמשאבים.
**ג. HbA1c גבוה.** מעיד על איזון סוכר לקוי, אך אינו מוכיח מי אחראי לכך.
**ד. הזיהוי בידי עוזרת הבית.** עיתוי הזיהוי מוסיף הקשר, אך כשלעצמו פחות ממוקד מהפער הקליני.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, נספח 1.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

q: אישה בת 84 עם יתר לחץ דם, כאב כרוני עקב היצרות עמוד השדרה, ו-MCI שאובחן לאחרונה, מגיעה עם בתה לחידוש מרשמים. היא נוטלת amlodipine 5mg, gabapentin 300mg TID, ו-acetaminophen PRN. הבת עונה על כל השאלות ומפסיקה את המטופלת בכל פעם שהיא מנסה לדבר. כשנשאלת על שליטה בכאב, המטופלת מתחילה לענות אך הבת מתערבת ואומרת 'היא בסדר, היא מתלוננת יותר מדי.' המטופלת מורידה את עיניה ומפסיקה לדבר. איזה סוג של התעללות הכי סביר במקרה זה?
o: התעללות כלכלית כלפי המטופלת
התעללות פסיכולוגית כלפי המטופלת
הזנחת הטיפול הרפואי במטופלת
פגיעה גופנית מכוונת במטופלת
explanation:
התעמרות נפשית יכולה להתבטא בהפחדה, השפלה או שליטה בדיבור. השתתקות בנוכחות המלווה מחייבת שיחה בפרטיות. **התעללות פסיכולוגית כלפי המטופלת**.

**א. התעללות כלכלית כלפי המטופלת.** לא תואר שימוש לא מורשה בכסף.
**ב. התעללות פסיכולוגית כלפי המטופלת.** דפוס ההפחדה והרתיעה מתאים לחשד לפגיעה נפשית.
**ג. הזנחת הטיפול הרפואי במטופלת.** אין תיאור של חסך בטיפול רפואי.
**ד. פגיעה גופנית מכוונת במטופלת.** ההתנהגות מעוררת חשד אך אינה כשלעצמה ראיה להפעלת כוח גופני.

אסמכתא · נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, נספח 1, עמ׳ 8 עד 9.
ref: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF p.8, Appendix 1, psychological mistreatment
label: Source: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF p.8, Appendix 1, psychological mistreatment

q: גבר בן 80, המוגדר חסר ישע, מאושפז שוב עקב החמרה באי־ספיקת לב. בנו אחראי למתן התרופות. אי־התאמות בטיפול ופחד של המטופל מבנו מעוררים חשד להזנחה בידי האחראי עליו. לצד בדיקה רפואית, הגנה ועירוב עובד סוציאלי, מהו סף חובת הדיווח לפקיד סעד או למשטרה המתואר בנוהל?
o: יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי
ממצא חד־משמעי בחקירה המוכיח עבירה בידי האחראי
הודאה מתועדת של האחראי בביצוע העבירה המדוברת
הסכמה חתומה של המשפחה להעברת החשד לרשויות
explanation:
חובת דיווח נועדה לאפשר לרשויות לברר חשד לפגיעה בחסר ישע בידי אדם אחראי. **יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי**.

**א. יסוד סביר לחשוב שנעברה עבירה בידי האחראי.** יסוד סביר מספיק להפעלת חובת הדיווח.
**ב. ממצא חד־משמעי בחקירה המוכיח עבירה בידי האחראי.** הוכחה פלילית היא תוצאה אפשרית של חקירה.
**ג. הודאה מתועדת של האחראי בביצוע העבירה המדוברת.** אין להתנות הגנה על הנפגע בהודאת החשוד.
**ד. הסכמה חתומה של המשפחה להעברת החשד לרשויות.** הסכמת המשפחה אינה תנאי לדיווח הקבוע בדין.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 2, 6, סעיפים 1.2, 8, 9.
ref: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF pp.2, 6, sections 1.2, 8–10
label: Source: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות · PDF pp.2, 6, sections 1.2, 8–10

q: An 84-year-old man has become slower and weaker over six months, has difficulty rising from chairs, and recently fell. He has lost weight unintentionally and has hypertension, diabetes and mild chronic kidney disease. Examination shows temporal wasting, low grip strength and slow gait. Which approach matches Hazzard's treatment principles for sarcopenia?
o: Resistance exercise with nutritional and protein support
Daily aerobic walking as a replacement for resistance exercise
Growth hormone treatment to restore muscle strength and function
Vitamin D supplementation as the principal sarcopenia treatment
explanation:
Difficulty rising from a chair reflects loss of lower-limb strength. **Combine progressive resistance exercise with adequate nutrition and protein** to train force production while supplying substrate for muscle maintenance.

**A. Resistance exercise plus nutrition.** These address both the training stimulus and nutritional needs.
**B. Walking as a replacement.** Aerobic activity is complementary but does not replace progressively loaded muscle contractions.
**C. Growth hormone.** An increase in mass need not translate into safer transfers or better strength.
**D. Vitamin D as principal treatment.** Correct deficiency when present. Vitamin D alone does not provide the required strengthening stimulus.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 737.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA

q: בדיון בישראל על טיפול בחולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות, אך אינו בשלב סופי, נקבע רצונו כדין. המשפחה מבקשת להבין מה פירוש "טיפול נלווה" בסעיף 16 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות. איזה תיאור מתאים?
o: טיפול שאינו קשור כלל למחלה חשוכת המרפא
טיפול שנועד להאריך חיים באמצעות טיפול במחלה חשוכת המרפא
טיפול שנבחר לפי מידת הפולשנות בלי קשר למחלה שבגללה ניתן
טיפול המוגדר לפי המקום שבו ניתן, בקהילה או באשפוז
explanation:
הסיווג תלוי בקשר בין מטרת הטיפול למחלה חשוכת המרפא. אצל חולה חסר כשרות שאינו בשלב הסופי יש להבחין בין טיפול במחלה לבין הטיפול הנלווה. **טיפול שאינו קשור כלל למחלה חשוכת המרפא**.

**א. טיפול שאינו קשור כלל למחלה חשוכת המרפא.** טיפול בבעיה אחרת נכלל בהגדרה, לפי מצבו הרפואי של החולה.
**ב. טיפול שנועד להאריך חיים באמצעות טיפול במחלה חשוכת המרפא.** זהו טיפול במחלה שבגללה נקבע שהחולה נוטה למות.
**ג. טיפול שנבחר לפי מידת הפולשנות בלי קשר למחלה שבגללה ניתן.** פעולה פולשנית יכולה להידרש דווקא לטיפול במחלה אחרת.
**ד. טיפול המוגדר לפי המקום שבו ניתן, בקהילה או באשפוז.** אותה פעולה יכולה להיות טיפול נלווה בבית ובבית חולים.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו-2005 עמ׳ 10.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A woman with moderate Alzheimer disease takes immediate-release memantine 10 mg twice daily. Her creatinine clearance is 22 mL/min. Which adjustment matches the Hazzard dosing table?
o: Reduce the dose to 5 mg twice daily
Combine the doses into 20 mg once daily
Continue 10 mg twice daily with food
Continue 10 mg twice daily without food
explanation:
Memantine is cleared substantially by the kidneys. For the immediate-release formulation, severe renal impairment changes the target dose.

**Reduce to 5 mg twice daily.** A creatinine clearance of 22 mL/min lies in the 5 to 29 mL/min range for this lower target.

**A. 5 mg twice daily.** This halves the total dose from 20 to 10 mg daily while retaining the immediate-release schedule.
**B. 20 mg once daily.** Combining both doses leaves the excessive daily exposure unchanged and gives a larger single dose.
**C. 10 mg twice daily with food.** Food does not correct reduced renal clearance.
**D. 10 mg twice daily without food.** The formulation may be taken without food, but the dose still needs reduction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 913, Table 59-7.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: A 77-year-old man hospitalized for a heart-failure exacerbation becomes confused at night, fails to recognize his wife and tries to leave, although he was alert and oriented that morning. His regular drugs are lisinopril, carvedilol and spironolactone; zolpidem was added three weeks ago. Assessment shows acute onset, inattention and disorganized thinking with normal alertness. Which approach addresses a potentially modifiable contributor?
o: Review zolpidem withdrawal and introduce nonpharmacologic sleep measures
Order head imaging first while continuing the recently added hypnotic unchanged
Start scheduled daytime haloperidol before attempting environmental interventions

explanation:
Orthostatic hypotension is a fall in blood pressure after standing. This patient's pressure drops by 32 mm Hg systolic and 14 mm Hg diastolic at the same time that he becomes dizzy.

**B. Review dopaminergic treatment.** Relating falls and dizziness to standing and dosing can help guide a supervised adjustment.
**C. Assume motor wearing-off.** Wearing-off causes predictable return of motor symptoms before a dose. Here the immediate clue is the documented postural pressure drop.

**B. Abundant regional blood supply makes nonunion unlikely after displacement.** The abundant, redundant blood supply is more characteristic of the intertrochanteric region.

**A. Wait for peak pain.** Repeated peaks can impair movement and make relief slower.

**C. Therapy sessions only.** The pain is present outside rehabilitation sessions.
**D. Scheduled treatment.** Cover the baseline pattern, reassessing relief and sedation before adjusting doses.

q: An 83-year-old woman regained independence after a hip fracture but avoids walking outside because she fears falling. Which possible sequence is described by Hazzard?
o: Avoidance of daily activities followed by reduced mobility and frailty
Avoidance of daily activities followed by improved mobility and endurance
Avoidance of daily activities followed by a reduction in physical frailty
Avoidance of daily activities followed by improved independence in daily function
explanation:
After a hip fracture, confidence may recover more slowly than walking ability. **Fear-driven avoidance can reduce mobility and lead to frailty**, even after independence initially returns.

**A. Avoidance, then reduced mobility.** Less walking can weaken balance, endurance and willingness to undertake daily tasks.
**B. Avoidance, then greater endurance.** Reducing activity limits the exercise stimulus needed to maintain capacity.
**C. Avoidance, then less frailty.** Prolonged restriction can diminish reserve and increase vulnerability.
**D. Avoidance, then more independence.** Loss of community mobility can narrow daily function even if indoor tasks remain possible.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 633.

q: A 78-year-old man is admitted from primary care with three days of acute confusion, unsteadiness, and falls. Six weeks earlier he underwent right hip ORIF, complicated by postoperative delirium that resolved. Discharge medications included tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed and vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Laboratory results are Na 124, K 3.8, creatinine 1.1, and glucose 98. Which assessment of tramadol is supported by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Review tramadol for its SIADH and hyponatremia risks
Continue tramadol as a treatment that counters SIADH-related hyponatremia
Increase tramadol because its sodium-related risk is a rise in sodium
Continue tramadol because sodium monitoring is unrelated to starting this drug
explanation:
Tramadol can cause or worsen inappropriate antidiuresis and hyponatremia. A recent change in cognition or balance can be a presenting clue to low sodium.

**Review tramadol as a contributor to the sodium of 124.** Evaluate the hyponatremia promptly and check the timing of actual doses rather than assuming a single cause.

**A. Review for SIADH and hyponatremia.** The drug can contribute to water retention and a fall in serum sodium.
**B. Continue as treatment for SIADH.** Tramadol can worsen the disturbance and has no role in correcting it.
**C. Increase because sodium may rise.** The relevant adverse effect is a low sodium concentration.
**D. Continue without sodium monitoring.** Sodium deserves close monitoring when tramadol is started or its dose changes.

q: After rehabilitation for a hip fracture, a woman is independent in feeding and dressing. You now want to assess her ability to maintain an independent household. Which activities are instrumental activities of daily living?
o: Managing medications, paying bills, and preparing meals
Bathing, putting on clothes, and feeding herself
Transferring from bed, using the toilet, and grooming
Maintaining continence, bathing, and transferring to a chair
explanation:
**Managing medications, paying bills and preparing meals** are instrumental ADLs. They assess the more complex skills required to live independently in the community.

**A. Medicines, finances and meals.** All three require organization and household management.
**B. Bathing, clothing and feeding.** These are basic self-care activities.
**C. Transferring, toileting and grooming.** These are basic mobility or self-care tasks.
**D. Continence, bathing and transfers.** This group also measures basic ADLs.

q: A patient takes calcium carbonate as a calcium supplement. Which advice about administration and bowel effects agrees with Hazzard?
o: Take it with food and monitor for constipation
Take it while fasting and monitor for constipation
Take it with food and expect relief of constipation
Take it while fasting and expect relief of constipation
explanation:
Calcium carbonate is absorbed better with food and can worsen constipation. **Take calcium carbonate with a meal and monitor bowel symptoms**.

**A. With food and watch for constipation.** This combines appropriate administration with a common adverse effect.
**B. Fasting and watch for constipation.** The bowel advice fits, but fasting is less favorable for carbonate absorption.
**C. With food for constipation relief.** Food is appropriate. Calcium carbonate can aggravate constipation rather than relieve it.

q: An 82-year-old long-term-care resident with cognitive impairment and urinary incontinence needs help toileting. The team wants a nighttime plan that protects sleep. Which approach follows Hazzard?
o: Wake him for scheduled toileting even during uninterrupted sleep
Provide incontinence care at each night check even when he is asleep
Individualize nighttime care and offer toileting when he is found awake
Use the daytime toileting schedule at night even when it interrupts sleep
explanation:
Assisted toileting can reduce wet episodes in residents with cognitive impairment, but repeated nighttime waking disrupts sleep. **Individualize nighttime care and offer toileting when he is awake**, while attending promptly to discomfort or skin needs.

**A. Wake for every scheduled void.** A rigid schedule interrupts uninterrupted sleep whether or not he needs to void.
**B. Provide care at every check.** Automatic intervention can cause avoidable awakenings. Assess actual care needs.
**C. Prompt when awake.** This provides access to the toilet without routinely waking him.
**D. Copy the daytime schedule.** Daytime strategies should be adapted to nighttime sleep and the resident's voiding pattern.

q: A 75-year-old woman is being reviewed for osteoporosis one year after a hip fracture. She completed five years of alendronate before the fracture. Her hip T-score is now −1.3, previously −2.9; calcium is 9.6 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73 m², and 25-hydroxyvitamin D 35 ng/mL. She has difficulty remembering daily medication but reliably attends a weekly bridge club. During discussion of treatment options, which drug binds RANKL to inhibit osteoclast activation?
o: Zoledronic acid given by intravenous infusion
Teriparatide given by daily subcutaneous injection
Denosumab given by subcutaneous injection
Alendronate given as oral bisphosphonate treatment
explanation:
RANKL is a signal that promotes osteoclast formation and activity. **Denosumab binds RANKL and reduces bone resorption**. The mechanism identifies the drug, while kidney function, calcium balance and follow-up matter separately to treatment choice.

**A. Zoledronic acid.** This intravenous bisphosphonate is retained in bone and inhibits osteoclast activity by another pathway.
**B. Teriparatide.** Intermittent parathyroid hormone receptor stimulation promotes bone formation.
**C. Denosumab.** This monoclonal antibody blocks RANKL before it activates its receptor on osteoclast-lineage cells.
**D. Alendronate.** It is an oral bisphosphonate, not a RANKL-binding antibody.

q: An 88-year-old man in rehabilitation has lost weight and eats little. He dislikes his restrictive diet but eats preferred foods well. No swallowing disorder is found. Which food-based approach matches Hazzard recommendations for improving oral intake?
o: Offer preferred foods and minimize restrictions with dietitian support
Offer less-preferred foods and maintain restrictions with dietitian support
Reduce meal frequency and maintain restrictions with dietitian support
Narrow the choice of foods and strengthen restrictions with dietitian support
explanation:
Poor intake during rehabilitation can reflect an unappealing therapeutic diet. This man eats his favorites and swallows normally, so **offer preferred foods and remove unnecessary restrictions with dietitian support**.

**A. Preferred foods and fewer restrictions.** This addresses the demonstrated barrier and can improve energy and protein intake.
**B. Less-preferred foods and the same restrictions.** Dietitian involvement will not make a menu that he avoids effective.
**C. Fewer meals and continuing restrictions.** Fewer opportunities to eat compound the problem. Small meals and snacks may be more manageable.
**D. Narrower choices and tighter restrictions.** They further reduce access to foods he is willing to eat.

q: An 80-year-old woman has lost walking ability after hip-fracture repair and can participate in rehabilitation. What should guide selection of the rehabilitation setting after discharge?
o: Functional loss, participation, support, and patient preferences
Implant design and body weight as the main placement determinants
Age and type of surgery as the decisive placement determinants
Radiographic implant position as the decisive placement determinant
explanation:
Rehabilitation placement matches the intensity of skilled therapy and support to the patient's recovery needs. **Use functional loss, ability to participate, available support and her preferences**.

**A. Functional and personal factors.** Loss of walking creates a therapy goal. Participation and support determine where it can realistically be pursued.
**B. Implant and weight.** These may affect handling or loading but do not measure therapy tolerance or home support.
**C. Age and operation.** People of the same age after the same procedure can have very different abilities.
**D. Implant position.** A satisfactory radiograph cannot show whether she can transfer safely or manage at home.

q: An 84-year-old man is medically stable after a stroke and able to participate in rehabilitation. Assessment finds no delirium or active depression, but he struggles to see how exercises will help. He previously enjoyed woodworking. Which approach could help motivation according to Hazzard?
o: Increase exercise volume without linking it to a personal goal
Postpone rehabilitation until motivation returns on its own
Set measurable goals in an activity important to the patient
Assign exercises in a fixed sequence shared by all patients
explanation:
A patient is more likely to practice a difficult movement when he understands what it will let him do again. Breaking a meaningful activity into measurable steps makes progress visible.

**Agree on a measurable goal connected to woodworking, such as safely reaching for and grasping a familiar tool, then link the exercise to that goal.**

**A. Increase exercise volume.** More repetitions without a purpose he recognizes do little to address his reluctance.
**B. Wait for motivation to return.** He is stable and able to participate. Choosing a meaningful, achievable first step gives him a reason to begin now.
**C. Set measurable goals in a valued activity.** Success on a small woodworking-related task shows him how the movement transfers to something he wants to do.
**D. Use the same sequence for everyone.** A fixed sequence ignores his interests and the particular movements he needs to regain.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 821.

q: An older woman develops delirium after hip surgery. Alongside evaluation and treatment of medical causes, which environmental approach follows Hazzard?
o: Encourage orientation, family contact, and use of sensory aids
Limit family presence to reduce exposure to familiar stimuli
Change rooms and care staff frequently to renew attention
Use bed restraints to reduce the risk of confusion
explanation:
Supportive delirium care helps restore orientation and compensates for impaired hearing or vision. Familiar people can explain where the patient is and what is happening.
**Include family, repeat orienting cues and use the patient's glasses or hearing aids.**

**A. Encourage orientation, family contact, and use of sensory aids.** These interventions improve access to environmental information without adding sedation.
**B. Limit family presence to reduce exposure to familiar stimuli.** Familiar contact can ease fear and provide useful baseline history.
**C. Change rooms and care staff frequently to renew attention.** Frequent changes make the environment harder to recognize.
**D. Use bed restraints to reduce the risk of confusion.** Restricting movement can increase agitation and functional decline.

q: An 81-year-old man in cardiac rehabilitation reports dizziness on standing. Assessment identifies several contributors, including medications and impaired vision. Which management principle is appropriate?
o: Attribute the symptoms to one medication and defer assessment of other contributors
Add a medicine for dizziness before reviewing the existing medication regimen
Correct the visual impairment without addressing the other contributing factors
Address modifiable contributors and review potentially contributing medications
explanation:
Dizziness in an older adult often has several interacting causes. **Address the impaired vision and review potentially contributory medications**, while assessing the blood-pressure response to standing.

**A. Assume one drug explains everything.** A single attribution misses other demonstrated contributors to unsteadiness.
**B. Add a dizziness drug first.** This increases medication burden before potentially reversible adverse effects have been evaluated.
**C. Correct vision alone.** Better visual input may help balance, but a postural medication effect could persist.
**D. Address modifiable contributors.** Match each intervention to a finding and reassess symptoms during rehabilitation.

q: A 79-year-old woman with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, and a recent L2 compression fracture is in skilled rehabilitation. She has progressed from a wheelchair to walking 100 ft with a walker but has had two near-falls while reaching. She leans heavily on the walker and has difficulty shifting weight sideways. HbA1c is 7.2% and vitamin D is 28 ng/mL. During review of exercise approaches, which description identifies tai chi as presented in Hazzard?
o: Group practice of leaning, multidirectional weight shifts, and coordinated breathing
Individual home practice of prescribed balance, strengthening, and walking exercises
Daily-life integration of balance and strength tasks whenever an opportunity arises
Group balance and functional training supplemented by a prescribed home exercise program
explanation:
Tai chi trains controlled postural movement and balance. **Coordinated leaning and multidirectional weight shifts with breathing, often practiced in a group**, identify it among these exercise approaches.

**A. Group weight shifts with breathing.** This combines the movement and breathing features characteristic of tai chi. Suitability depends on her current abilities.
**B. Individual home strengthening and walking.** This describes a prescribed home-exercise approach.
**C. Tasks integrated into daily life.** Practicing balance or strength whenever a daily task permits characterizes the LiFE program.
**D. Group training plus home prescriptions.** This describes a hybrid group and home exercise program rather than the defining tai chi movements.

q: גבר בן 85 נמצא ביום 3 של שיקום אקוטי לאחר החלפת שני ברכיים. יש לו CKD stage 3 (eGFR 45), CHF (EF 40%), ואוסטאופורוזיס. הוא מוטיבציה אך מפתח כאב קשה (9/10) עם כיפוף הברך מעבר ל-70 מעלות, המגביל את התקדמות הטיפול. טיפול אנלגטי נוכחי: acetaminophen 1g TID, celecoxib 200mg יומי, oxycodone 5mg q6h PRN (משתמש ב-3-4 מנות ביום). אשתו שואלת על תרופות כאב חזקות יותר. מהי ההתאמה המתאימה ביותר?
o: להעלות oxycodone ל-7.5mg q6h PRN
להוסיף gabapentin 100mg TID
להחליף celecoxib ב-naproxen 250mg BID
להוסיף tramadol 25mg q6h
explanation:
The listed answer is **low-dose gabapentin**, an adjunct for neuropathic pain. Here the pain is provoked by knee flexion and no neuropathic features are described. Reassess the joint and rehabilitation plan before adding a sedating drug.

**A. Increase oxycodone.** A higher dose can worsen sedation, falls and constipation. Review timing relative to therapy and evaluate disproportionate pain.
**B. Add gabapentin.** There is a rationale for renal-adjusted gabapentin if neuropathic pain is demonstrated. Concomitant oxycodone increases sedation and respiratory risk.
**C. Switch to naproxen.** Systemic NSAIDs can worsen heart failure and kidney function. A switch from celecoxib does not remove those risks.
**D. Add tramadol.** Adding a second opioid increases adverse effects and complicates assessment of benefit.

q: A 77-year-old woman with dementia is undergoing rehabilitation after hip-fracture repair. She becomes agitated when staff move the affected limb and cannot answer pain questions consistently. Which approach is appropriate for assessing pain?
o: Use an observational pain scale and obtain additional information from caregivers
Defer pain assessment until language improves enough for a detailed interview
Use broad questions about general well-being instead of specific pain questions
Require completion of a numerical intensity scale before interpreting pain symptoms
explanation:
Pain assessment in dementia combines attempted self-report with observable responses. **Use an observational pain scale and caregiver information** for agitation when the repaired limb is moved.

**A. Observe and ask caregivers.** Facial expression, guarding or vocalization during movement may reveal pain.
**B. Wait for language recovery.** Communication difficulty may persist and should not delay treatment.
**C. General questions.** Simple, specific questions about the painful movement are more informative.
**D. Require a numerical score.** A patient may experience substantial pain despite inability to use a rating scale.

q: A man with Parkinson disease has recurrent rigidity before each levodopa dose, followed by a good response and no peak-dose dyskinesia. The team plans to alter the frequency of the same formulation before adding a drug. Which change fits wearing-off?
o: Lengthen the intervals between daytime doses
Delay each dose until rigidity has begun
Move the daytime doses to nighttime administration
Shorten the intervals between daytime doses
explanation:
Wearing-off means that the benefit of a levodopa dose ends before the next one takes effect. The patient's repeated return of rigidity followed by good relief from each dose is a timing clue.

**Shorten the interval between daytime doses.** Giving the next dose sooner can narrow the period in which levodopa no longer controls his rigidity.

**A. Lengthen the intervals.** This would extend the symptomatic gap he already experiences.
**B. Wait for rigidity.** Deliberately waiting leaves him immobile before each dose has time to take effect.
**C. Shift daytime doses to night.** This does not cover the daytime periods in which rigidity returns.
**D. Shorten the intervals.** The medicine still works at each dose. The problem is that its benefit does not last to the next one.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 944–945.

q: A 76-year-old woman starting resistance training reports severe muscle soreness and prolonged generalized fatigue after each session. How should this affect the next exercise prescription?
o: Maintain the load and lengthen the session to promote adaptation
Add a session between workouts to reduce recovery days
Reduce the load and adjust it according to monitored responses
Increase resistance and shorten rest periods to improve strength
explanation:
Resistance training stimulates adaptation when the challenge is followed by recovery. Repeated severe soreness and prolonged generalized fatigue suggest that the current load exceeds this patient’s recovery capacity.

**Reduce the load and use her symptoms during exercise and the following day to guide subsequent progression.**

**A. Maintain load and lengthen sessions.** Adding work increases the dose that is already causing excessive symptoms.
**B. Add a session between workouts.** Reducing recovery days makes it less likely that fatigued muscles will recover before the next challenge.
**C. Reduce load and monitor.** A lower starting dose with adequate rest allows productive practice. Advance when the patient tolerates the current work without severe next-day symptoms.
**D. Increase resistance and shorten rests.** Both changes increase stress when a reduction is indicated.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 824–825.

q: An 83-year-old woman with COPD experiences dyspnea during rehabilitation. Which breathing modification is described in Hazzard as a way to reduce the sensation of breathlessness?
o: Pursed-lip breathing with a shortened exhalation phase
Pursed-lip breathing with a prolonged exhalation phase
Open-mouth breathing with a shortened exhalation phase
Faster-rate breathing with a shortened exhalation phase
explanation:
Breathing retraining can reduce perceived breathlessness in COPD. **Pursed-lip breathing with prolonged exhalation** gives more time for lung emptying during rehabilitation.

**A. Pursed lips and short expiration.** Shortening the phase loses the intended expiratory benefit.
**B. Pursed lips and prolonged expiration.** A slow, controlled breath out can help reduce air trapping.
**C. Open mouth and short expiration.** This lacks the controlled expiratory pattern.
**D. Faster breathing.** Short rapid breaths can worsen dynamic hyperinflation.

q: An older adult treated with insulin develops impaired vision and hand dexterity. Before selecting a self-monitoring device, what should be assessed according to Hazzard?
o: Ability to monitor glucose and manage hypoglycemia
Chronological age as the basis for device selection
HbA1c as evidence of independent device operation
Family preference as evidence of independent device operation
explanation:
Monitoring is useful only if a patient can obtain a result, read it and act on it safely. Vision and hand dexterity can limit each of these tasks.

**Assess the ability to monitor glucose and manage hypoglycemia before selecting a device.** Have the patient demonstrate the steps and identify the help needed.

**A. Assess monitoring and response.** These functional skills determine whether the device will protect the patient when glucose falls.
**B. Choose by chronological age.** People of the same age vary widely in vision, dexterity, cognition and support.
**C. Infer ability from A1C.** An average glucose marker cannot show whether a screen is readable or a lancet usable.
**D. Infer ability from family preference.** Caregiver preferences can inform the choice, but independent operation requires actual demonstration.

q: An 86-year-old woman with dementia has difficulty remembering exercises during rehabilitation after a fracture. She cooperates with guidance, and her daughter wishes to help. Which approach should guide rehabilitation goals?
o: Set goals jointly, considering the patient’s abilities and family support
Set goals from the patient’s age, using standard exercise norms
Set goals from the memory score, using cognitive screening results
Set goals from the fracture site, using the findings on follow-up radiographs
explanation:
Memory impairment can make an exercise sequence difficult to remember, even when the patient can follow a demonstration. Rehabilitation goals should reflect the activities she wants to recover and the help she can use to practice them.

**Set goals with the patient and her daughter, using her observed abilities and the daughter’s capacity to cue practice.**

**A. Joint goals based on ability and support.** A transfer she can learn with a consistent prompt is an achievable functional target. Her daughter can reinforce the same cue outside therapy.
**B. Age and standard norms.** Age does not reveal which tasks she can relearn or which activities matter to her.
**C. Memory score alone.** A cognitive score does not show how she performs a task with demonstration, repetition or family guidance.
**D. Fracture site and radiographs.** These guide precautions and healing expectations, but cannot define her functional goals or how to practice them.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 817, 820–821.

q: A 78-year-old man with postoperative iron-deficiency anemia stopped an adequate oral iron regimen because of substantial intolerance. He is stable and has no active bleeding. Which method of iron replacement is supported by Hazzard?
o: Continue the same oral preparation despite the substantial intolerance.
Postpone iron replacement until he has completed his rehabilitation.
Give intravenous iron instead of the intolerable oral regimen.
Give erythropoietin instead of replacing the documented iron deficit.
explanation:
Stable postoperative iron deficiency can be treated without transfusion when there is no ongoing bleeding or ischemia. **Give IV iron after substantial oral intolerance** to restore iron needed for erythropoiesis.

**A. Continue the same oral formulation.** Poor tolerance has already prevented an adequate course.
**B. Wait for rehabilitation to finish.** A suitable replacement route is available while recovery proceeds.
**C. Replace iron intravenously.** This supplies the missing substrate without requiring the intolerable tablets.
**D. Use erythropoietin alone.** Erythropoietin does not replenish depleted iron stores.

q: An 81-year-old woman in rehabilitation after a pelvic fracture practices transfers and balance. Which goal describes a functional outcome in daily life rather than a measure of exercise performance?
o: Improve rising from a chair and mobility in daily life
Increase the number of repetitions completed during each exercise session
Increase the duration of exercise completed during each treatment session
Increase the joint range of motion measured during an exercise
explanation:
A functional goal describes an activity the patient can perform in daily life. Repetitions, exercise time and joint range can help track progress toward that activity.

**Rising from a chair and moving around in daily life are functional outcomes because they describe useful transfers and mobility outside the treatment session.**

**A. Chair rise and everyday mobility.** Being able to get up and move about changes what she can do at home and how much assistance she needs.
**B. Number of repetitions.** This measures how much exercise she completed. More repetitions need not mean that she can transfer safely.
**C. Duration of a session.** Time spent exercising measures treatment exposure and tolerance. It does not tell whether she can rise from a chair.
**D. Measured joint range.** Range is a physical attribute. Her daily outcome depends on using that range together with strength and balance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 818–819, 823.

q: גבר בן 77 עם פרקינסון ודיספאגיה מבין את סיכון האספירציה ואת חלופות ההזנה, ומסוגל לקבל החלטה. הוא מבקש לאכול דרך הפה, ואשתו מתנגדת. אין מצב חירום ואין החלטה המתירה חריגה מכללי ההסכמה. לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה, על בחירתו של מי יש לבסס את ההחלטה לאחר מסירת המידע?
o: על בחירת המטופל, לאחר שהבין את הסיכונים ואת החלופות
על בחירת אשתו, המשמשת מטפלת עיקרית ומכירה את מצבו
על בחירת הרופא, המעריך את התועלת ואת הסיכון הרפואי
על בחירת צוות השיקום, המעריך את מטרות ההזנה והשיקום
explanation:
כאשר המטופל מסוגל להבין את צורת ההזנה ואת החלופות, ההחלטה מצריכה את הסכמתו מדעת. **על בחירת המטופל, לאחר שהבין את הסיכונים ואת החלופות**.

**א. על בחירת המטופל, לאחר שהבין את הסיכונים ואת החלופות.** הוא שוקל את הסיכון והתועלת בהתאם למטרותיו.
**ב. על בחירת אשתו, המשמשת מטפלת עיקרית ומכירה את מצבו.** תפקיד האישה כמטפלת אינו מקנה סמכות להחליפו.
**ג. על בחירת הרופא, המעריך את התועלת ואת הסיכון הרפואי.** הרופא מציע ומסביר ואינו בוחר בשם מטופל כשיר.
**ד. על בחירת צוות השיקום, המעריך את מטרות ההזנה והשיקום.** הצוות מעריך את הבטיחות ויכול להתאים את התוכנית.

q: During a preoperative assessment, the team plans to use the Clinical Frailty Scale. Which description matches the scale in Hazzard?
o: A nine-level functional scale incorporating activity and dependence.
A five-level laboratory scale incorporating inflammatory measurements.
A thirty-point cognitive scale incorporating memory and language.
A three-level nutritional scale incorporating weight and intake.
explanation:
The Clinical Frailty Scale summarizes baseline fitness, activity and dependence for daily tasks. **It is a nine-level clinical scale**, ranging from very fit through severe frailty to terminal illness.

**A. Nine functional levels.** Activity and help needed with instrumental and basic tasks inform the rating.
**B. Five laboratory levels.** Inflammatory laboratory markers do not define the CFS.
**C. Thirty-point cognitive scale.** That format resembles the MMSE rather than a frailty rating.
**D. Three nutritional levels.** Weight and intake alone cannot characterize multidimensional frailty.

q: An 84-year-old man in rehabilitation after hip surgery develops acute confusion and stops participating in therapy. Renal impairment and electrolyte disturbances are present, and he is receiving an opioid. Which management approach is appropriate?
o: Increase the opioid to restore participation in rehabilitation
Add a stimulant to overcome fatigue during rehabilitation
Add a sleep medication to improve cooperation with therapy
Assess and treat delirium causes, including medications
explanation:
New inability to participate in rehabilitation may be an early sign of delirium. Kidney dysfunction, electrolyte imbalance and medication effects can act together.
**Evaluate and treat the contributing illness and medication effects before targeting participation itself.**

**A. Increase the opioid to restore participation in rehabilitation.** Increasing an opioid without pain or exposure assessment risks worsening sedation.
**B. Add a stimulant to overcome fatigue during rehabilitation.** A stimulant does not correct kidney dysfunction or electrolyte imbalance.
**C. Add a sleep medication to improve cooperation with therapy.** A hypnotic can increase inattention and further impair participation.
**D. Assess and treat delirium causes, including medications.** Clinical assessment can identify several modifiable factors and guide rehabilitation as attention recovers.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 881–882, 885

q: A woman after a stroke can transfer to a commode, but cognitive impairment prevents her from requesting help in time. There are no signs of infection or urinary retention. Staff are available to help. Which intervention is appropriate?
o: Emphasize independently performed pelvic floor muscle exercises
Emphasize a bladder diary maintained by the patient herself
Provide assisted toileting at regularly scheduled intervals
Emphasize independently lengthening the intervals between voids
explanation:
The patient can transfer with help but cannot remember to ask for it. **Initiate assisted toileting at regular intervals** so bladder emptying does not depend on her requesting help.

**A. Emphasize independently performed pelvic floor muscle exercises.** Independent exercises require learning and address outlet control rather than access.
**B. Emphasize a bladder diary maintained by the patient herself.** Keeping her own diary requires memory and initiation she does not reliably have.
**C. Provide assisted toileting at regularly scheduled intervals.** Staff can help with transfers before leakage occurs. The absence of infection or retention supports a behavioral approach.
**D. Emphasize independently lengthening the intervals between voids.** Self-directed interval training similarly depends on her ability to plan and remember.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 710, 709.

q: An older adult has persistent pain after orthopedic surgery that worsens during physical therapy. A surgical complication has been excluded. Which pain-regimen plan matches Hazzard's approach to supporting rehabilitation?
o: Give analgesia on request after pain appears during exercise
Concentrate analgesia at night to improve the patient's rest
Give sustained analgesia without adjusting for therapy sessions
Provide sustained relief and anticipate pain during therapy
explanation:
Pain management after hip fracture surgery should enable movement as well as comfort at rest. **Provide baseline relief and anticipate pain during physiotherapy.**

**A. Give analgesia on request after pain appears during exercise.** Waiting for pain during exercise can interrupt the session before treatment takes effect.
**B. Concentrate analgesia at night to improve the patient's rest.** Nighttime-only treatment misses movement-related pain during daytime rehabilitation.
**C. Give sustained analgesia without adjusting for therapy sessions.** Baseline treatment helps, but breakthrough pain during a predictable activity also warrants planning.
**D. Provide sustained relief and anticipate pain during therapy.** Time suitable analgesia before therapy and reassess its effect on both participation and adverse effects.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 797.

q: A 77-year-old woman has iron-deficiency anemia. Which follow-up finding supports changing to intravenous iron under the recommendations in Hazzard’s anemia chapter?
o: Anemia improves with oral iron, which she takes without adverse effects
Oral iron has not been tried, and she can take it by mouth
Anemia does not improve with oral iron despite taking it regularly
Anemia improves with oral iron, but she requests an infusion because of her age
explanation:
An inadequate hemoglobin response despite properly taken oral iron warrants reassessment for ongoing losses or malabsorption. **Persistent anemia despite adherence** also supports changing to IV replacement.

**A. Improves and tolerates tablets.** Effective, well-tolerated treatment provides no failure or intolerance indication.
**B. Oral iron never tried.** If safe and absorbable, oral iron is a reasonable starting route.
**C. No response despite adherence.** IV treatment bypasses absorption limitations while the reason for inadequate response is investigated.
**D. Improves but requests IV because of age.** Age alone is not a medical indication to replace a working oral regimen.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.
ref: Hazzard Ch 94 — AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA
chapterTitle: AGING OF THE HEMATOPOIETIC SYSTEM AND ANEMIA

q: An opioid-naive 85-year-old woman with dementia and chronic kidney disease has persistent pain limiting rehabilitation despite nonopioid treatment. After assessment, a trial of an opioid is chosen. Which initiation principle matches Hazzard?
o: Begin with an extended-release formulation to reduce dosing frequency
Begin at the usual younger-adult dose for rapid analgesia
Begin at a low dose with close monitoring of response
Begin treatment and defer adverse-effect assessment to a distant visit
explanation:
An opioid-naive older adult with CKD and dementia is particularly vulnerable to accumulation and confusion. **Begin with a low dose of an appropriate immediate-release opioid and monitor closely**.

**A. Extended release initially.** Long exposure makes early dose adjustments harder.
**B. Younger-adult starting dose.** Reduced clearance may make that exposure excessive.
**C. Low dose and close review.** Assess comfort, rehabilitation participation, alertness and breathing.
**D. Distant review.** Early toxicity can develop before a delayed appointment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1060.

q: A person with Parkinson disease responds well to each levodopa dose, but stiffness and slowness recur before each daytime dose. There is no significant dyskinesia. The initial plan is to adjust the timing of the existing formulation. Which change addresses this end-of-dose problem?
o: Lengthen the interval between daytime doses
Combine daytime doses into a single bedtime dose
Reduce the number of daytime doses to limit fluctuations
Shorten the interval between daytime doses
explanation:
End-of-dose wearing-off is recognizable by stiffness and slowness returning on a predictable schedule, then improving again after levodopa. Peak-dose dyskinesia would appear while the medicine is exerting its strongest effect.

**Give daytime levodopa more frequently.** Shorter intervals match the schedule to the shorter duration of benefit without changing formulations.

**A. Lengthen daytime intervals.** A longer gap increases the time spent stiff before the next dose.
**B. Combine doses at bedtime.** A single nighttime dose provides no reliable coverage for repeated daytime off periods.
**C. Give fewer daytime doses.** Fewer opportunities to renew the response leave more of the day uncovered.
**D. Shorten daytime intervals.** This anticipates the return of symptoms while preserving the motor response to each dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 944–945.
ref: Hazzard Ch 61 — PARKINSON DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS

q: An 82-year-old woman develops inattention, confusion, and fluctuating alertness after hip surgery. Gabapentin appears on her medication list, but its start date and any recent dose changes are unknown. Which diagnostic approach is appropriate?
o: Attribute the confusion to lingering anesthesia effects
Attribute the confusion to psychosis and initiate targeted treatment
Attribute the confusion to gabapentin from the drug list
Investigate delirium contributors, including medication changes
explanation:
A medication list is a starting point for assessing exposure. The timeline of surgery, illness, doses and changes is necessary to judge a drug's contribution.
**Investigate postoperative delirium and reconstruct the medication history, including any gabapentin change.**

**A. Attribute the confusion to lingering anesthesia effects.** Anesthesia is one possibility among several and cannot be assigned as the sole cause from timing alone.
**B. Attribute the confusion to psychosis and initiate targeted treatment.** Fluctuating attention and arousal suggest a medical syndrome.
**C. Attribute the confusion to gabapentin from the drug list.** A listed medication may be relevant, but its presence does not show that it caused this episode.
**D. Investigate delirium contributors, including medication changes.** Clarifying actual doses and timing helps evaluate drug effects along with pain, hypoxemia and metabolic disturbances.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 883–885

q: A 76-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and chronic back pain has become sedentary and mentally foggy despite physical therapy. He takes duloxetine, cyclobenzaprine, and acetaminophen. Which medication change removes a skeletal muscle relaxant that the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria recommend avoiding in older adults?
o: Increase duloxetine while continuing the current cyclobenzaprine prescription
Add modafinil while continuing the current cyclobenzaprine prescription
Discontinue cyclobenzaprine because of its adverse-effect profile
Increase acetaminophen while continuing the current cyclobenzaprine prescription
explanation:
Cyclobenzaprine is a skeletal muscle relaxant used for musculoskeletal symptoms. Older adults may develop sedation and anticholinergic effects at doses with uncertain benefit.

**Discontinue cyclobenzaprine.** Removing it addresses a plausible contributor to mental fog and reduces exposure associated with fractures.

**A. Increase duloxetine.** A change in analgesic treatment leaves the sedating muscle relaxant in place.
**B. Add modafinil.** Countering drowsiness pharmacologically can add a prescribing cascade while the possible cause continues.
**C. Stop cyclobenzaprine.** This removes the muscle relaxant whose adverse effects are directly relevant to the new functional complaints.
**D. Increase acetaminophen.** Additional analgesia does not remove cyclobenzaprine’s central or anticholinergic effects.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2063.

q: An 83-year-old woman with systolic heart failure is receiving spironolactone. Which monitoring pair is especially important during initiation and dose titration because of this drug’s risks?
o: Serum sodium and thyroid function
Serum calcium and coagulation studies
Blood glucose and liver enzyme levels
Serum potassium and renal function
explanation:
The essential monitoring pair for spironolactone is **serum potassium and renal function**. Check both at initiation, after dose changes and when illness or interacting drugs alter risk.

**A. Sodium and thyroid tests.** Sodium can matter in heart failure, but thyroid testing does not monitor the main MRA hazard.
**B. Calcium and coagulation.** Neither reflects impaired potassium excretion.
**C. Glucose and liver enzymes.** These do not identify the characteristic renal and electrolyte complication.
**D. Potassium and renal function.** Declining filtration increases the likelihood of dangerous hyperkalemia during mineralocorticoid receptor blockade.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 76, p. 1181.

q: A 79-year-old man is undergoing rehabilitation after a severe illness. Nutritional assessment identifies unintentional weight loss and inadequate energy and protein intake. An oral nutritional supplement is added to meals and rehabilitation. How should it be incorporated to increase daily intake?
o: Give the supplement with meals to concentrate energy intake
Give the supplement instead of meals to simplify intake
Give the supplement between meals to limit reduced food intake
Give an appetite stimulant instead of the nutritional supplement
explanation:
Rehabilitation increases the importance of meeting energy and protein needs. **Give the oral supplement between meals** so that it adds to daily intake while minimizing displacement of normal food.

**A. With meals.** A supplement alongside food may increase fullness before the meal is finished.
**B. Instead of meals.** Replacement can negate the intended addition to calories and reduce dietary variety.
**C. Between meals.** A separate serving creates another opportunity to receive energy and protein.
**D. Appetite stimulant instead.** Drug-induced appetite or weight changes do not reliably improve function, and such drugs can cause adverse effects.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 428.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: אישה בת 80 עם פרקינסון לאחר שבר ירך מתקדמת לאט בשיקום. המשפחה מבקשת לדעת כיצד יוחלט על המשך התוכנית ועל השחרור. מה נדרש לפי חוזר משרד הבריאות?
o: לקבוע את ההמשך לפי התפקוד שתואר לפני השבר
לקבוע את ההמשך לפי מספר השבועות שחלפו מהניתוח
להעריך מחדש ולהתאים תוכנית לצרכים ולהתקדמות
לקבוע את ההמשך לפי האבחנה הנוירולוגית הראשית
explanation:
שיקום הוא תהליך שמעריכים לאורך זמן. לקראת שחרור משווים את ההתקדמות ליעדים ובודקים אילו תמיכות עדיין נחוצות. **להעריך מחדש ולהתאים תוכנית לצרכים ולהתקדמות**.

**א. לקבוע את ההמשך לפי התפקוד שתואר לפני השבר.** התפקוד הקודם הוא נקודת השוואה ולא תוצאת השיקום.
**ב. לקבוע את ההמשך לפי מספר השבועות שחלפו מהניתוח.** חלוף זמן בלבד אינו מלמד אם היעד הושג.
**ג. להעריך מחדש ולהתאים תוכנית לצרכים ולהתקדמות.** הערכה חוזרת מדריכה התאמת תוכנית וטיפול המשך.
**ד. לקבוע את ההמשך לפי האבחנה הנוירולוגית הראשית.** שם האבחנה אינו מתאר את יכולת ההליכה והעזרה הנדרשת כעת.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר 4/2009, סעיפים 8.4–8.5, עמ׳ 7.

q: An older adult with stable type 2 diabetes is being considered for oral treatment. There is no acute illness, unstable heart failure, or renal contraindication. Which statement describes the principal glucose-lowering action of metformin in Hazzard?
o: It primarily promotes insulin release from pancreatic beta cells
It primarily delays absorption of glucose from intestinal contents
It primarily suppresses glucose production within the liver
It primarily increases excretion of glucose through the kidneys
explanation:
The liver releases glucose between meals, and excess hepatic output contributes to fasting hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes. Metformin targets that process without directly forcing insulin secretion.

**Metformin chiefly suppresses hepatic glucose production.** It can also improve insulin-mediated peripheral glucose uptake.

**A. Promotes beta-cell insulin release.** This is the principal mechanism of sulfonylureas and glinides.
**B. Delays intestinal glucose absorption.** Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors slow carbohydrate digestion and blunt postmeal peaks.
**C. Suppresses hepatic glucose output.** This is the main mechanism of metformin and helps explain its low intrinsic risk of hypoglycemia.
**D. Increases urinary glucose excretion.** SGLT2 inhibitors cause this effect by reducing proximal tubular glucose reabsorption.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1576–1577, Table 99-11.

q: A woman with dementia and a painful fracture continues to show signs of pain despite an adequate trial of acetaminophen. What can be considered next under the stepwise pain-treatment approach described in Hazzard?
o: Consider an antipsychotic as the initial treatment for persistent pain
Consider waiting for a detailed verbal report before changing treatment
Consider discontinuing analgesics because the patient has a dementia diagnosis
Consider an opioid trial while assessing the patient’s response
explanation:
Pain in dementia may be expressed by guarding, grimacing or distress during movement. After inadequate acetaminophen for a fracture, **consider a monitored opioid trial**.

**A. Antipsychotic for pain.** It can mask behavior without relieving nociceptive pain.
**B. Wait for a detailed report.** Cognitive impairment may make verbal description impossible.
**C. Stop analgesics.** Dementia increases the risk of undertreated pain.
**D. Opioid trial.** Assess observed comfort and function alongside sedation, constipation and other harms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1048.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 75-year-old man with COPD presents for pulmonary rehabilitation. His oxygen saturation is 92% at rest and 86% while walking. According to Hazzard, which additional finding supports oxygen use during exertion in this setting?
o: An expected reduction in hospital admissions inferred from the exercise saturation
An expected improvement in lung function inferred from the resting saturation
Improved dyspnea or exercise capacity demonstrated during a trial of oxygen
An expected survival improvement inferred from the low walking saturation
explanation:
Exertional oxygen is intended to improve symptoms or function during activity in appropriately selected patients. **Demonstrate better dyspnea or exercise capacity during an oxygen trial** when saturation falls to 86% with walking.

**A. Fewer admissions assumed.** An exercise saturation alone cannot predict hospitalization benefit.
**B. Better lung function assumed.** Oxygen does not reverse airflow obstruction.
**C. Observed exercise benefit.** Compare symptoms or walking performance on oxygen while documenting exertional desaturation.
**D. Longer survival assumed.** Survival evidence for severe chronic resting hypoxemia cannot simply be transferred to isolated exertional desaturation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1257.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 1257, Supplemental oxygen

q: An 81-year-old woman with low vision from macular degeneration is practicing stair climbing in rehabilitation. Which environmental adjustment will help her identify the step edges?
o: Paint the step edges in a color similar to their background
Create a transition from a bright room to a dark stair corridor
Mark the step edges with tape that contrasts with their background
Place a light source that produces a bright reflection on the stairs
explanation:
Step edges are easier to detect when they stand out from the tread. **Apply contrasting tape to the edges**, under adequate, even lighting.

**A. Matching paint.** Similar colors obscure the boundary between separate surfaces.
**B. Bright-to-dark transition.** Slower dark adaptation can temporarily make the stairway harder to see.
**C. Contrasting tape.** The edge remains distinguishable even when visual detail is poor.
**D. Bright reflected light.** Glare may mask the edge and reduce useful contrast.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 482–483.
ref: Hazzard Ch 33 — LOW VISION: ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION

q: A 78-year-old man with dementia and falls takes oxybutynin. The team decides to remove the strongly anticholinergic drug from his regimen and plan treatment of urinary incontinence separately. Which action achieves that aim?
o: Discontinue treatment with oxybutynin
Replace treatment with solifenacin
Replace treatment with tolterodine
Replace treatment with trospium
explanation:
Oxybutynin is a bladder antimuscarinic with strong anticholinergic properties. Other medicines in the same class can preserve that exposure when substituted.

**Discontinue oxybutynin and assess incontinence separately.** This achieves the team’s goal of removing a strong anticholinergic.

**A. Stop oxybutynin.** Withdrawal removes the current exposure without introducing another bladder antimuscarinic.
**B. Replace with solifenacin.** Solifenacin is also strongly anticholinergic.
**C. Replace with tolterodine.** Tolterodine continues muscarinic blockade and warrants cognitive caution.
**D. Replace with trospium.** Trospium also belongs to the strongly anticholinergic bladder drug group, even though individual agents differ.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2074.

q: An 84-year-old woman has dysuria and urinary frequency without fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Urine culture grows E. coli susceptible to nitrofurantoin, ciprofloxacin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate but resistant to TMP-SMX. Which oral agent is the appropriate first-line choice for acute simple cystitis according to Hazzard?
o: Ciprofloxacin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
Nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
TMP-SMX as first-line treatment based on the clinical diagnosis
Amoxicillin-clavulanate as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
explanation:
Acute simple cystitis causes bladder symptoms without signs of kidney or systemic infection. Her isolate is susceptible and creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. **Nitrofurantoin is a first-line oral option** in this setting.

**A. Ciprofloxacin.** Susceptibility does not make a fluoroquinolone the preferred option when an effective narrower first-line agent is suitable.
**B. Nitrofurantoin.** It reaches effective urinary levels and her clearance is above the 30 mL/min threshold used here.
**C. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.** The isolate is resistant.
**D. Amoxicillin-clavulanate.** It may be an alternative in selected circumstances, but it is not the preferred first-line choice among these options.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1708–1709.

q: For which stage of Alzheimer disease does Hazzard explicitly describe an approved indication for memantine?
o: Alzheimer disease with moderate-to-severe dementia
Early Alzheimer disease with mild dementia
Mild cognitive impairment before dementia develops
Subjective memory concerns without objective impairment
explanation:
Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist used for symptomatic treatment as Alzheimer dementia advances. The indication depends on clinical severity and daily impairment.

**Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer dementia** is the stage in which memantine is indicated.

**A. Moderate-to-severe dementia.** Modest benefits in cognition, function or behavior make this the appropriate disease stage.
**B. Mild dementia.** A diagnosis of early Alzheimer dementia alone does not supply the established memantine indication.
**C. Mild cognitive impairment.** Independence is preserved, and memantine has no established role in preventing conversion to dementia.
**D. Subjective memory concern.** First determine whether objective decline or functional impairment exists.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 911.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: A woman with dementia becomes restless during bathing. There is no immediate danger, and behavioral intervention has not yet been tried. Which initial approach is appropriate?
o: Introduce a sedative as preparation for bathing sessions
Adapt the care approach and try nonpharmacologic measures
Introduce an antipsychotic as the first symptom intervention
Increase sleep medication as the first bathing intervention
explanation:
Restlessness during bathing is linked to a particular activity and there is no immediate danger. **Adapt the care routine and try nonpharmacologic measures first.**

**A. Introduce a sedative as preparation for bathing sessions.** Sedation before each bath carries fall and delirium risks and leaves triggers unexplored.
**B. Adapt the care approach and try nonpharmacologic measures.** Assess discomfort, preserve privacy, offer choices and try a different caregiver, timing or technique.
**C. Introduce an antipsychotic as the first symptom intervention.** An antipsychotic is not an appropriate first response to uncomplicated resistance to care.
**D. Increase sleep medication as the first bathing intervention.** More sleep medication has no direct rationale for a bathing-specific behavior.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 925.
ref: Hazzard Ch 60 — BEHAVIORAL SYMPTOMS OF DEMENTIA AND PSYCHOACTIVE DRUG THERAPY
chapterTitle: Behavioral Symptoms of Dementia and Psychoactive Drug Therapy

q: A man with Alzheimer disease and diabetes receives basal insulin once daily but makes dosing errors and sometimes misses meals. His daughter can help. Which adjustment directly addresses safe implementation of his existing regimen?
o: Provide written instructions and continue independent insulin administration.
Add glucose measurements and continue independent insulin administration.
Supervise insulin administration and observe actual meal intake.
Split insulin injections and continue independent dose calculation.
explanation:
Insulin safety depends on the actual dose administered and the patient's food intake. Cognitive impairment can disrupt both even when a prescription is simple.

**Have the daughter supervise insulin administration and observe meals.** This targets the documented dosing errors and missed meals that increase hypoglycemia risk.

**A. Written instructions.** The patient may read the plan and still forget a dose, repeat it or miss a meal.
**B. More glucose checks.** Readings can detect a problem, but they do not ensure that insulin and meals are managed safely.
**C. Supervise the dose and meals.** Observe what is actually given and eaten, then use that information to review whether the regimen needs adjustment.
**D. Split injections.** More dosing steps and calculations compound the execution problem.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 916.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: אישה בת 83 עם דמנציה מתקדמת מסוג אלצהיימר (MMSE 8/30) מאושפזת מבית אבות עם דלקת ריאות משאיפה. היא ירדה 15% ממשקל גופה במהלך 6 חודשים וזקוקה לסיוע מלא בהאכלה. היא אינה מזהה עוד את בני משפחתה. בהערכה של ריפוי בעיסוק או קלינאות תקשורת תועדה הפרעת בליעה חמורה עם שאיפת נוזלים דקים. בנה שואל לגבי הכנסת צינור הזנה. בהנחיות המקדימות שלה נכתב שהיא מסרבת להזנה מלאכותית. איזו תגובה מתייחסת בצורה הטובה ביותר למטרות הטיפול?
o: להסביר שהכנסת PEG היא דרך למנוע אספירציה נוספת אצל המטופלת
להסביר שהאכלה ידנית זהירה דורשת התאמה של המרקם והערכת הבליעה
להציע זונדה זמנית כדרך ההזנה במהלך הטיפול הנוכחי בדלקת הריאות
להמליץ על מעבר מיידי להוספיס כתגובה לבקשת הבן בעניין ההזנה
explanation:
החלטה על הזנה מחייבת שיחה עם המשפחה על מטרות המטופל, מצבו הקליני והפער בין הזנה לבין מניעת שאיפה. **להסביר שהאכלה ידנית זהירה דורשת התאמה של המרקם והערכת הבליעה**.

**א. להסביר שהכנסת PEG היא דרך למנוע אספירציה נוספת אצל המטופלת.** PEG אינו מבטל שאיפת רוק או תוכן קיבה.
**ב. להסביר שהאכלה ידנית זהירה דורשת התאמה של המרקם והערכת הבליעה.** בהאכלה ידנית מתאימים מרקם, קצב ותנוחה לפי הערכת הבליעה.
**ג. להציע זונדה זמנית כדרך ההזנה במהלך הטיפול הנוכחי בדלקת הריאות.** הכנסת זונדה אינה עונה כשלעצמה לשאלה מה מתבקש להשיג.
**ד. להמליץ על מעבר מיידי להוספיס כתגובה לבקשת הבן בעניין ההזנה.** בקשת הבן אינה התוויה אוטומטית למעבר להוספיס.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית בעניין הזנה לחולה עם קיהיון, עמ׳ 3 עד 6.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A woman with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis has not yet tried an anti-inflammatory medication and wants topical treatment before an oral drug. Which rationale supports topical diclofenac according to Hazzard?
o: Deep penetration that makes it particularly suitable for hip osteoarthritis
Broad systemic action that makes it suited to many affected joints
Pain relief with a favorable adverse-effect profile
Cartilage modification that replaces the need for symptom treatment
explanation:
Topical diclofenac delivers anti-inflammatory treatment to an accessible joint with lower systemic exposure than an oral NSAID. **Pain relief with a favorable adverse-effect profile** supports trying it first for localized knee osteoarthritis.

**A. Especially suitable for the deep hip.** Depth limits effective topical delivery to the hip joint.
**B. Broad systemic effect for many joints.** Treating numerous sites topically is less practical. Systemic exposure is intentionally reduced.
**C. Local relief, fewer systemic effects.** This benefit is particularly relevant when renal, cardiovascular or gastrointestinal adverse effects are a concern.
**D. Repairs cartilage.** Diclofenac treats symptoms and does not restore cartilage or reverse osteoarthritis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 787–788.

q: An 80-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia and atrial fibrillation is reviewed after a mechanical fall at home. His wife reports increasing confusion over the past two weeks and difficulty managing medications. He takes warfarin with a target INR of 2-3, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. His INR today is 4.8, without active bleeding. After addressing the current INR abnormality, the clinician is considering a direct oral anticoagulant for longer-term stroke prevention. Which principle should guide this assessment?
o: Select a direct anticoagulant and defer renal assessment until bleeding develops.
Assess renal function when selecting and monitoring the direct oral anticoagulant regimen.
Favor full-dose dabigatran when gastrointestinal bleeding risk is a treatment concern.
Treat coexisting stroke and bleeding risks as grounds for withdrawing anticoagulation.
explanation:
After the supratherapeutic INR and change in cognition are addressed, **assess renal function before selecting a DOAC and during follow-up**. Confirm eligibility, interactions and the ability to take the regimen reliably.

**A. Defer renal assessment.** Renal clearance influences drug choice and dose before the first prescription.
**B. Check renal function.** Use the agent-specific prescribing criteria. Arrange help with adherence when cognition affects medication use.
**C. Prefer full-dose dabigatran for GI bleeding risk.** High-dose dabigatran can increase gastrointestinal bleeding in susceptible patients.
**D. Withdraw because both risks exist.** Bleeding and stroke risks often coexist. Address modifiable hazards and individualize treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 77, pp. 1202–1205.

q: A woman with dementia develops confusion and hallucinations over several days after starting a sleep medication. She poses no danger to herself. What is the appropriate initial approach?
o: Increase the sleep medication to reduce the hallucinations
Assess delirium causes and review the new medication
Add an antipsychotic before evaluating the cause of confusion
Attribute the change to dementia and defer acute evaluation
explanation:
New hallucinations in someone with dementia can reflect an acute superimposed syndrome. Sleep drugs may contribute by altering alertness and attention.
**Search for delirium precipitants and review the newly started sleep medication.**

**A. Increase the sleep medication to reduce the hallucinations.** Increasing the dose risks worsening a potentially drug-related episode.
**B. Assess delirium causes and review the new medication.** The several-day course calls for medication reconciliation and medical assessment.
**C. Add an antipsychotic before evaluating the cause of confusion.** With no immediate danger, adding an antipsychotic before evaluating causes exposes her to unnecessary harm.
**D. Attribute the change to dementia and defer acute evaluation.** Dementia raises susceptibility. It does not make new symptoms expected or remove the need for acute assessment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–885, 888

q: A patient with delirium and severe agitation has not improved with nonpharmacologic measures. After assessment, cautious antipsychotic treatment is selected. What is the clinical treatment endpoint described in Hazzard?
o: A patient who remains asleep throughout the daytime
A patient whose alertness is reduced for many hours
A patient who is awake and manageable
A patient who does not respond to external stimulation
explanation:
Antipsychotics used for delirium are titrated to manage a safety threat. Excess sedation interferes with monitoring the underlying illness.
**The desired endpoint is wakefulness with behavior that allows safe care.**

**A. A patient who remains asleep throughout the daytime.** Daytime sleep prevents meaningful assessment and participation.
**B. A patient whose alertness is reduced for many hours.** Sustained reduction in alertness represents oversedation.
**C. A patient who is awake and manageable.** An awake patient who can accept care has reached the behavioral goal.
**D. A patient who does not respond to external stimulation.** Absent responses indicate a dangerously excessive effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 889

q: מטופלת מאושפזת בישראל מוגדרת חסרת ישע. בבירור עולה חשד שהאדם האחראי עליה פוגע בה. איזה צעד מתחייב לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות?
o: דחיית ההודעה עד לפגישה משותפת עם המטפל ועם המשפחה
מסירת הודעה מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה על החשד
המתנה לאימות סופי של האירוע לפני העברת הודעה לגורם חיצוני
הסתפקות במעקב מחלקתי ובתיעוד במקום מסירת הודעה חיצונית
explanation:
יסוד סביר לחשוד בפגיעה בחסרת ישע בידי האחראי עליה מחייב הודעה לגורם הקבוע בדין. **מסירת הודעה מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה על החשד**.

**א. דחיית ההודעה עד לפגישה משותפת עם המטפל ועם המשפחה.** פגישה משפחתית אינה תנאי ועלולה להגביר סיכון.
**ב. מסירת הודעה מיידית לפקיד סעד או למשטרה על החשד.** ההודעה מועברת לעו״ס לפי חוק או למשטרה, במקביל לטיפול.
**ג. המתנה לאימות סופי של האירוע לפני העברת הודעה לגורם חיצוני.** בירור סופי הוא מתפקידי הגורמים החוקרים.
**ד. הסתפקות במעקב מחלקתי ובתיעוד במקום מסירת הודעה חיצונית.** רישום פנימי אינו ממלא את חובת ההודעה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, סעיף 8.5, עמ׳ 6.
