q: An 84-year-old man with knee osteoarthritis still has pain that limits walking despite topical and oral treatment. Which statement about a local intervention is supported by Hazzard?
o: Hyaluronic acid injections have clear benefit after trial bias is addressed
TNF inhibitor injections are recommended for treating erosive osteoarthritis
Corticosteroid injections provide short-term relief of pain from knee osteoarthritis
Mesenchymal stem cell injections are approved for routine osteoarthritis care
explanation:
Intra-articular treatment can provide symptom relief when knee osteoarthritis limits mobility despite usual therapy. **A corticosteroid injection can reduce pain in the short term**.

**A. Hyaluronic acid.** Apparent benefit is less convincing when trial bias is addressed.
**B. TNF inhibitor.** Biologic anti-TNF treatment is not standard for erosive osteoarthritis.
**C. Corticosteroid injection.** Discuss temporary relief, with no assured long-term benefit.
**D. Stem-cell injection.** This remains investigational for routine OA care.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 788–789, 1067.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 1067

q: A 79-year-old woman with an osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture asks when vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty is considered in Hazzard. Which situation supports considering it?
o: Persistent severe pain attributed to the fracture despite conservative care
New severe fracture pain before a trial of conservative care
Persistent severe pain with a burst fracture and retropulsed bone
Persistent severe pain with an uncorrected coagulation disorder
explanation:
Vertebral augmentation is a procedure for selected painful osteoporotic vertebral fractures. **Consider it when severe pain clearly attributable to the fracture persists despite appropriate conservative care**, after assessing contraindications.

**A. Persistent fracture pain despite care.** Persistent disabling pain localized to the affected level is the relevant indication for assessment.
**B. New pain before conservative care.** Initial management generally includes analgesia and measures to preserve mobility.
**C. Burst fracture with retropulsion.** Retropulsed bone changes the anatomical risks and is a contraindication to routine augmentation.
**D. Uncorrected coagulopathy.** Bleeding risk must be addressed and can preclude a procedure despite severe pain.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1066, 1638.

q: An 81-year-old man with diabetes and peripheral neuropathy has worsening burning foot pain for three months. He takes metformin, lisinopril, and aspirin; HbA1c is 8.2%, and monofilament sensation is absent bilaterally. He lives alone and recently stopped driving because of pain. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily caused severe dizziness. Which listed analgesic option belongs to the serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor class?
o: Pregabalin
Duloxetine
Amitriptyline
Capsaicin
explanation:
SNRIs increase serotonin and norepinephrine signaling and may relieve neuropathic pain. **Duloxetine is the SNRI** among the proposed treatments for burning diabetic foot pain.

**A. Pregabalin.** A gabapentinoid acting at a calcium-channel subunit.
**B. Duloxetine.** Its dual reuptake inhibition modulates pain pathways. Individual suitability still requires clinical assessment.
**C. Amitriptyline.** A tricyclic antidepressant with substantial anticholinergic effects.
**D. Capsaicin.** A topical agent acting at peripheral nociceptors.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1063, 1064.

q: A 77-year-old woman with chronic low-back pain has marked lumbar facet arthropathy on MRI, local facet tenderness, and pain on extension and lateral rotation. She has hypertension and osteoporosis and takes amlodipine, alendronate, and acetaminophen. Physical therapy gave little relief, and tramadol caused nausea. Which description of medial branch blocks agrees with Hazzard?
o: They target nerves supplying the facet joints to provide diagnostic information
They target nerves supplying the facet joints and demonstrate arthropathy severity on imaging
They target the vertebral body and test whether a compression fracture causes pain
They target the sacroiliac joint space and test whether sacroiliac pain is present
explanation:
A medial branch block tests whether a lumbar facet joint contributes to pain. **It targets the medial branch nerves supplying the facet joints and provides diagnostic information**.

**A. Facet nerve supply.** Temporary relief supports a facet-mediated component.
**B. Imaging severity.** A block tests the pain generator. MRI describes anatomy.
**C. Vertebral body.** Compression fractures involve the vertebral body, a different target.
**D. Sacroiliac joint.** That joint requires a different localization and assessment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1066.
ref: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p. 1066, Facet joint injections; p. 1064, Table 68-8

q: A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?
o: Begin an initial therapeutic trial of acetaminophen
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an antipsychotic
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an opioid
Wait for a detailed verbal description of the pain
explanation:
Unrecognized pain can appear as agitation in dementia. **Start the described stepwise empiric protocol with acetaminophen** and assess behavior and comfort.

**A. Acetaminophen trial.** A scheduled trial can reveal whether pain relief improves distress.
**B. Antipsychotic first.** Suppressing agitation does not treat a painful cause.
**C. Opioid first.** The protocol reserves escalation for inadequate initial analgesia, while severe acute pain warrants individual assessment.
**D. Wait for detailed self-report.** Use behavioral signs and caregiver observations when communication is impaired.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1048.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 73-year-old man receiving an opioid for chronic pain develops somnolence and confusion. His renal function is impaired. Which mechanism explains increased susceptibility to adverse effects?
o: Reduced medication clearance with prolonged drug exposure
Increased medication clearance with shortened drug exposure
Reduced risk of central nervous system depression with aging
Unchanged drug exposure despite the decline in renal function
explanation:
Some opioids or active metabolites persist longer when renal function is impaired. **Reduced clearance prolongs exposure and can cause somnolence and confusion**.

**A. Reduced clearance.** Reconsider the agent, dose, interval and other sedating medicines.
**B. Increased clearance.** This would usually shorten exposure.
**C. Aging protects the CNS.** Older patients are more sensitive to sedation and cognitive effects.
**D. Unchanged exposure.** Renal impairment can materially alter drug or metabolite concentrations.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1060.

q: An 80-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis has recurrent pain rated 7/10 that limits shopping. A course of three hyaluronic acid injections six months ago initially helped. She has heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and stage 3b CKD, and takes furosemide, lisinopril, and carvedilol. Examination shows an effusion and crepitus. She is reluctant to undergo the knee replacement recommended by her surgeon. Which injectable option has evidence for symptomatic relief in Hazzard, while the other choices are described as lacking clear benefit or remaining experimental?
o: Intra-articular injection using hyaluronic acid
Intra-articular injection using a glucocorticoid
Intra-articular injection using platelet-rich plasma
Intra-articular injection using mesenchymal stem cells
explanation:
Intra-articular glucocorticoid injection can provide short-term relief for a persistently painful osteoarthritic knee. **A glucocorticoid injection** is a reasonable local option with an effusion, after evaluating for other causes of swelling.

**A. Hyaluronic acid.** Her prior subjective relief matters to the discussion, but controlled evidence of consistent benefit is unclear.
**B. Glucocorticoid.** Local anti-inflammatory action can improve symptoms without the systemic kidney and heart-failure risks of an oral NSAID.
**C. Platelet-rich plasma.** Preparations vary, and expected pain relief is less predictable than with an intra-articular glucocorticoid.
**D. Mesenchymal stem cells.** These remain experimental for this indication and are not the established pain-relieving injection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 788–789.

q: A 78-year-old man has severe right-sided trigeminal neuralgia in the V2 distribution. He stopped gabapentin 300 mg three times daily because of delirium and has stopped shaving and eating solid food because of pain. He also has mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and type 2 diabetes treated with metformin and glyburide. Which block does Hazzard specifically list for V2 trigeminal neuralgia?
o: Inferior alveolar block for trigeminal pain in the V3 distribution
Posterior superior alveolar block for pain in the V2 distribution
Occipital nerve block for occipital neuralgia or cervicogenic headache
Sphenopalatine ganglion block for treatment of cluster headaches
explanation:
Trigeminal nerve blocks are chosen according to the painful facial distribution. **A posterior superior alveolar block targets a branch of V2** for selected maxillary-distribution neuralgia.

**A. Inferior alveolar.** This is a mandibular V3 branch.
**B. Posterior superior alveolar.** It arises from the maxillary division, matching the stated V2 distribution.
**C. Occipital.** This addresses posterior scalp pain or selected cervicogenic headache.
**D. Sphenopalatine ganglion.** It has a different indication, including selected cluster headache treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1067.

q: An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?
o: Use a short treatment trial and reassess whether pain relief justifies continuation
Escalate beyond the recommended daily limit when the initial response is small
Continue prolonged treatment and reserve liver monitoring for another drug exposure
Reject an individual treatment trial because average trial benefits were small
explanation:
Acetaminophen has modest average benefit in osteoarthritis but may help selected individuals. **Use a short, monitored trial and continue only if pain or function improves**, while investigating the new generalized pain and delirium.

**A. Short trial and reassessment.** Observe pain behavior during movement and care, particularly when dementia limits self-report.
**B. Exceed the daily maximum.** Limited benefit is a reason to reconsider therapy, not to increase hepatotoxicity risk.
**C. Continue without liver monitoring.** Prolonged use warrants attention to total daily exposure and hepatic safety.
**D. Reject every individual trial.** Small average effects do not exclude meaningful benefit in a particular patient.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 787.

q: A 75-year-old man with symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis asks about epidural steroid injection. Which result matches the randomized trial in Hazzard comparing glucocorticoid plus lidocaine with lidocaine injection?
o: Little added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with lidocaine injection
Little added short-term benefit compared with an uninjected control
Substantial added short-term benefit compared with decompressive surgery
explanation:
Epidural injections are used for leg pain from lumbar spinal stenosis. Both randomized groups received lidocaine, so the comparison isolated the contribution of the glucocorticoid. **Adding steroid offered little additional benefit at six weeks.**

**A. Little benefit beyond lidocaine.** The groups had similar outcomes for both leg pain intensity and pain-related disability.
**B. Substantial benefit beyond lidocaine.** At six weeks the groups differed by only 0.2 points in average leg pain on a scale from zero to ten.
**C. Little benefit over no injection.** Everyone received an epidural injection, leaving its benefit over no procedure unanswered.
**D. Substantial benefit over surgery.** Decompression relieves anatomic narrowing. The trial had no surgical comparison group.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1639. Friedly et al., N Engl J Med 2014, vol. 371, pp. 11–21.
ref: Hazzard Ch 102 — BACK PAIN AND SPINAL STENOSIS

q: An 86-year-old woman has marked vulvovaginal discomfort during personal care. Examination shows severe atrophy, dryness, and fissures without infection or a suspicious lesion. She has no contraindication to local estrogen. Which treatment is preferred for the symptomatic atrophy?
o: Low-dose oral gabapentin for pain in the vulvar region
Topical lidocaine before care for pain in the vulvar region
Low-dose vaginal estrogen for the symptomatic atrophic tissue
Vaginal moisturizer as primary treatment for severe symptomatic atrophy
explanation:
Estrogen deficiency can make vulvovaginal tissue dry, thin and prone to painful fissures. **Low-dose vaginal estrogen** addresses the tissue changes causing severe symptoms when no contraindication is present.

**A. Gabapentin.** It may treat neuropathic pain, but the examination identifies atrophy as the cause here.
**B. Topical lidocaine.** Anesthetic relief during care does not restore the atrophic tissue.
**C. Vaginal estrogen.** Local therapy improves mucosal health and targets the underlying estrogen deficiency.
**D. Moisturizer alone.** Nonhormonal moisturizers can help milder symptoms but may provide insufficient relief in severe atrophy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 534.

q: An older woman who received an opioid for pain has tablets left after she no longer needs them. According to Hazzard, what should counseling about these tablets include?
o: Keep the remaining tablets for another episode of similar pain
Plan how and where to dispose of the remaining tablets
Give the remaining tablets to a relative with similar pain
Store the remaining tablets for future use without discussing disposal
explanation:
Unused opioids are a risk for accidental ingestion and diversion. **Agree on a safe disposal plan**, such as returning tablets through an authorized take-back service.

**A. Keep the remaining tablets for another episode of similar pain.** Keeping tablets for a later illness bypasses reassessment of the cause and dose needed.
**B. Plan how and where to dispose of the remaining tablets.** A specific disposal plan reduces access once treatment has ended.
**C. Give the remaining tablets to a relative with similar pain.** Sharing a prescription exposes another person to an unassessed opioid dose and interactions.
**D. Store the remaining tablets for future use without discussing disposal.** Storage alone leaves unused opioid tablets accessible indefinitely.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 289.

q: An older woman with osteoporosis has sacral and buttock pain with local tenderness. Pelvic radiographs are negative, but suspicion of an insufficiency fracture remains high. Which principle follows Hazzard?
o: Plain radiograph sensitivity for small fractures can support ending evaluation
A normal neurologic examination can support lowering suspicion of a sacral fracture
Absence of a preceding fall can support lowering suspicion of a sacral fracture
MRI or CT can help document a small fracture despite negative radiographs
explanation:
An insufficiency fracture occurs when ordinary loading exceeds the strength of osteoporotic bone. **Persistent focal sacral pain after negative radiographs warrants MRI or CT.**

**A. Plain radiograph sensitivity for small fractures can support ending evaluation.** Small sacral fractures can be occult on plain films. A negative film does not adequately lower suspicion here.
**B. A normal neurologic examination can support lowering suspicion of a sacral fracture.** Sacral insufficiency fractures often cause pain without a neurologic deficit.
**C. Absence of a preceding fall can support lowering suspicion of a sacral fracture.** Fragile bone can fracture during ordinary activities without a fall.
**D. MRI or CT can help document a small fracture despite negative radiographs.** MRI can reveal marrow edema, while CT can delineate a fracture line.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1631.
ref: Hazzard Ch 102 — BACK PAIN AND SPINAL STENOSIS

q: An older woman has persistent neuropathic facial pain and cannot tolerate anticonvulsant treatment because of sedation. After appropriate assessment, a nerve block is considered. Which role does Hazzard describe for the block?
o: To identify a vascular lesion and assess trigeminal nerve compression
To identify an intracranial mass and guide its anatomical classification
To localize the pain source and reduce pain intensity or frequency
To localize the pain source and predict a permanent treatment response
explanation:
A targeted nerve block can help determine which nerve carries pain and can provide temporary relief. **Use it to localize the painful pathway and reduce pain intensity or frequency**.

**A. Vascular compression.** Trigeminal-protocol MRI can evaluate vascular contact.
**B. Mass classification.** Imaging characterizes an intracranial mass. A block cannot show its anatomy.
**C. Localization and relief.** The distribution and duration of response supply clinical information and symptom benefit.
**D. Permanent prediction.** A temporary response does not guarantee permanent relief.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1067.

q: An 81-year-old man has burning pain and allodynia in the left T10 dermatome six months after herpes zoster. Gabapentin and duloxetine have not helped. He has COPD, atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban, and stage 3 CKD; other medications are metoprolol, tiotropium, and acetaminophen. The pain prevents him from hugging his grandchildren. Which listed coanalgesic appears as a topical patch option in Hazzard’s Table 68-8?
o: Amitriptyline
Pregabalin
Lidocaine
Carbamazepine
explanation:
Burning allodynia limited to the previous zoster dermatome is postherpetic neuralgia. **Topical lidocaine** can target the painful area while limiting systemic exposure.

**A. Amitriptyline.** This systemic tricyclic can worsen anticholinergic burden and orthostasis.
**B. Pregabalin.** This is an oral gabapentinoid requiring renal adjustment.
**C. Lidocaine.** A lidocaine patch applied to intact skin is an option for localized postherpetic pain.
**D. Carbamazepine.** This systemic sodium-channel blocker is especially associated with trigeminal neuralgia.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 68, Table 68-8, pp. 1063–1064.

q: An 84-year-old man with COPD is hospitalized for an exacerbation with acute hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis. He is alert, cooperative, stable, and able to protect his airway, with no contraindication to mask ventilation. Which approach is appropriate in addition to medical therapy?
o: Provide conventional nasal oxygen and defer ventilatory support during treatment
Provide noninvasive positive pressure ventilation alongside ongoing medical treatment
Use systemic opioids for ventilatory support while continuing medical treatment
Use intravenous loop diuresis for ventilatory support during medical treatment
explanation:
Acute hypercapnic respiratory acidosis during a COPD exacerbation is a major indication for noninvasive ventilation. **Start mask positive-pressure ventilation alongside medical therapy** when the patient is cooperative, stable and protects the airway.

**A. Nasal oxygen alone.** It may correct hypoxemia but does not adequately assist ventilation in this setting.
**B. Noninvasive ventilation.** Pressure support reduces breathing work and helps correct hypercapnia and acidosis.
**C. Opioids as ventilation.** Opioids do not provide ventilatory support and can depress breathing.
**D. Loop diuretics as ventilation.** They treat congestion when present, not acute ventilatory muscle overload.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1257.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: A 78-year-old woman with moderate dementia (MMSE 18/30) has lost 8 kg in six months and now needs help bathing. She denies complaints. She takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 500 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 20 mg. Albumin is 2.8, hemoglobin 10.2, and TSH is normal. Her daughter asks about appetite stimulants. After reversible causes have been addressed, which approach is supported without assuming proven benefit from an appetite stimulant?
o: Use mirtazapine for weight gain without establishing depression.
Use megestrol for expected gains in function and quality of life.
Use dronabinol for established clinical benefits in older adults.
Adjust the meal environment and provide feeding assistance.
explanation:
Dementia can impair attention to food and the ability to initiate or finish a meal. Once reversible causes of weight loss are addressed, **adapt the dining environment and provide feeding assistance**.

**A. Mirtazapine solely for weight.** Evidence for weight benefit in the absence of depression is weak.
**B. Megestrol for function.** Any gain tends to be fat, with no demonstrated functional benefit and meaningful adverse effects.
**C. Dronabinol.** Small studies in older adults do not establish dependable clinical benefit.
**D. Feeding assistance.** Cueing, help with utensils and a suitable environment directly address barriers to eating.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 427–429.

q: An 81-year-old man with advanced illness wants relief of breathlessness while limiting medication burden. When should measures such as a fan and breathing techniques be introduced?
o: After the opioid dose has been increased to its maximum
After pharmacologic treatment for breathlessness has been stopped
After hypoxemia has been demonstrated by oxygen-saturation testing
As first-line measures alongside consideration of drug treatment
explanation:
A fan and breathing techniques are low-burden approaches to the sensation of dyspnea. **Introduce them early alongside consideration of medication**, matching the patient's wish to limit drug burden.

**A. Wait for maximum opioid dose.** Nonpharmacologic relief need not wait for dose escalation.
**B. Only after stopping medication.** The approaches can be combined.
**C. Wait for hypoxemia.** Breathlessness can respond to airflow or positioning despite normal saturation.
**D. First-line alongside drugs.** Assess comfort and continue the measures the patient finds helpful.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: A 79-year-old woman with dementia is hospitalized with pneumonia and develops delirium. She is stable and is not endangering herself. Which environmental adjustment is appropriate?
o: Concentrate nursing procedures at night with frequent awakenings
Display a clock and calendar and protect uninterrupted sleep
Change the room and staff frequently to encourage adaptation
Restrict movement in bed with physical restraints
explanation:
Orienting cues and a protected night are paired environmental interventions. A person with dementia may need repeated reminders in an unfamiliar ward.
**Keep a visible clock and calendar and coordinate care to permit uninterrupted sleep.**

**A. Concentrate nursing procedures at night with frequent awakenings.** Repeated nighttime awakenings can worsen the sleep disturbance.
**B. Display a clock and calendar and protect uninterrupted sleep.** The cues provide time and place information, while protected sleep supports daytime alertness.
**C. Change the room and staff frequently to encourage adaptation.** Unfamiliar rooms and changing carers increase disorientation.
**D. Restrict movement in bed with physical restraints.** Bed restraints reduce mobility and can worsen agitation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 888, Table 58-5

q: גבר עם דמנציה מתקדמת נושא הנחיות מקדימות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות בנוגע להזנה מלאכותית. בטרם מפעילים אותן כמסלול ההחלטה, איזה מצב דורש סעיף 31?
o: קביעת מצב חולה הנוטה למות וחוסר כשרות
קביעה שיש דמנציה מתקדמת ובת המוכנה להחליט
קביעה שיש קושי בבליעה ובקשת משפחה לצינור
קביעה שיש דלקת ריאות וצורך בתזונה זמנית
explanation:
**נקבע שהאדם חולה הנוטה למות ואינו בעל כשרות** לפני שמפעילים את ההנחיות לפי סעיף 31.

**א. שתי קביעות לפי החוק.** יש לבדוק גם תוקף מסמך ותחולה על הנסיבות והמזון או הנוזלים הנדונים.
**ב. דמנציה ובת המוכנה להחליט.** אינן מקיימות כשלעצמן את תנאי ההפעלה.
**ג. דיספגיה ובקשת צינור.** אלה נסיבות קליניות ומשפחתיות, ולא קביעת המעמד המשפטי.
**ד. דלקת ריאות והזנה זמנית.** אירוע חריף עשוי להיות הפיך ואינו מפעיל אוטומטית את המסמך.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 8 ו־31.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A 77-year-old woman with recurrent falls takes amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. Which adverse-effect profile explains the concern about its use in older adults in the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Cholinergic activity, sedation, and orthostatic hypotension
Anticholinergic activity, sedation, and orthostatic hypotension
Anticholinergic activity, stimulation, and an orthostatic blood-pressure rise
Cholinergic activity, stimulation, and an orthostatic blood-pressure rise
explanation:
Amitriptyline can impair thinking and alertness and lower blood pressure on standing. Together these effects are particularly hazardous in a patient with recurrent falls.

**The relevant combination is anticholinergic activity, sedation, and orthostatic hypotension.** All three can occur even when the indication is neuropathic pain.

**A. Cholinergic, sedating, hypotensive.** The latter two effects fit, but amitriptyline blocks muscarinic signaling.
**B. Anticholinergic, sedating, hypotensive.** Muscarinic blockade, drowsiness, and a postural pressure drop together increase functional risk.
**C. Anticholinergic, stimulating, pressure rise.** The drug can cause sedation and a fall in standing pressure.
**D. Cholinergic, stimulating, pressure rise.** All three proposed directions conflict with the effects that make amitriptyline problematic in older adults.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2059.

q: An 82-year-old man with lung cancer appears independent and has good performance status. Why is comprehensive geriatric assessment still useful before chemotherapy?
o: It substitutes the patient's functional age for the tumor and treatment variables in toxicity assessment
It confirms that a good performance score is sufficient for assessment before chemotherapy
It assigns physiologic and functional status from the patient's chronological age
It identifies vulnerabilities missed by routine oncology performance-status measures
explanation:
Independence on routine observation can conceal fall risk, malnutrition or cognitive difficulty. **Comprehensive geriatric assessment identifies vulnerabilities missed by oncology performance scores** before chemotherapy.

**A. Replace tumor and treatment information.** Toxicity assessment combines patient vulnerabilities with the planned regimen and cancer characteristics.
**B. ECOG is sufficient.** A favorable general activity score cannot rule out deficits in individual domains.
**C. Infer function from age.** Chronological age is a poor proxy for an individual patient's reserve.
**D. Find hidden vulnerabilities.** The results can change supportive care and the discussion of treatment intensity.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1386, 1387, 1388.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: An older woman with COPD and depression is being followed clinically. Which suicide-risk assessment is required as part of evaluating her depression?
o: Mood, sleep quality, appetite, and daily energy
Thoughts, intent, plans, and daily respiratory function
Thoughts, intent, plans, and access to lethal means
Past attempts, sleep quality, appetite, and family support
explanation:
Suicide-risk assessment explores current thoughts and whether the person might act on them. **Ask about suicidal thoughts, intent, plans and access to lethal means**.

**A. General depressive symptoms.** Sleep and appetite inform depression severity but omit immediate risk.
**B. Respiratory function.** COPD affects overall care but cannot substitute for asking about access to means.
**C. Thoughts, intent, plans and access.** These domains help determine urgency and protective measures.
**D. Past attempts and support.** Important background information still leaves current intent and plans unanswered.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1008.

q: בחולה עם דמנציה שהוגדר נוטה למות נשקלת דרך הזנה. מצבו מיוצב, והמשפחה מבקשת לדון באפשרויות. איזה עיקרון מנחה את קבלת ההחלטה לפי המלצות משרד הבריאות?
o: בחירת דרך הזנה לפי העדפת המוסד למסלול אחיד
בחירה רפואית אישית המותאמת לצרכים בשיתוף צוות רב־מקצועי
בחירת דרך הזנה לפי דרישת המשפחה להתקן קבוע
בחירת דרך הזנה לפי האבחנה בלי בחינת צרכים
explanation:
בחירת דרך הזנה בקיהיון היא החלטה רפואית מותאמת למטופל. מעריכים אפשרות לאכילה דרך הפה, סיכון בבליעה, צרכים והעדפות. **בחירה רפואית אישית המותאמת לצרכים בשיתוף צוות רב־מקצועי**.

**א. בחירת דרך הזנה לפי העדפת המוסד למסלול אחיד.** מדיניות אחידה אינה משקללת שונות בין דיירים.
**ב. בחירה רפואית אישית המותאמת לצרכים בשיתוף צוות רב־מקצועי.** הצוות משלב הערכת בליעה, תזונה ומצב רפואי עם יעדים אישיים.
**ג. בחירת דרך הזנה לפי דרישת המשפחה להתקן קבוע.** רצון המשפחה ראוי לדיון ואינו יוצר התוויה להתקן קבוע.
**ד. בחירת דרך הזנה לפי האבחנה בלי בחינת צרכים.** אבחנה בלי הערכת צרכים אינה מספיקה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, המלצות הוועדה הארצית על הזנה בחולה עם קיהיון, המלצות ד–ה, עמ׳ 5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: A 76-year-old man taking gabapentin for painful neuropathy has a creatinine clearance of 22 mL/min. Duloxetine is being considered. Which combination of decisions matches Table 6 of Beers 2023?
o: Increase gabapentin and avoid adding duloxetine
Reduce gabapentin and avoid adding duloxetine
Reduce gabapentin and start duloxetine
Increase gabapentin and start duloxetine
explanation:
Renal impairment does not affect every pain treatment in the same way. Gabapentin requires a lower dose to limit central adverse effects, whereas severe impairment increases gastrointestinal adverse effects with duloxetine.

**Reduce gabapentin and avoid starting duloxetine at 22 mL/min.** That creatinine clearance is below both the gabapentin reduction threshold of 60 and the duloxetine avoidance threshold of 30 mL/min.

**A. Increase gabapentin, avoid duloxetine.** Avoiding duloxetine fits this clearance, but more gabapentin increases the risk of accumulation.
**B. Reduce gabapentin, avoid duloxetine.** Both decisions account for the distinct adverse effects seen with impaired elimination.
**C. Reduce gabapentin, start duloxetine.** The gabapentin adjustment fits, but duloxetine is discouraged below 30 mL/min because of gastrointestinal adverse effects.
**D. Increase gabapentin, start duloxetine.** This increases CNS exposure from gabapentin while adding a drug discouraged at this clearance.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 6, p. 2073.
label: Source: AGS Beers 2023 · p.2073, Table 6 (PDF p.22)

q: A stable woman is evaluated for suspected pulmonary embolism. Clinical probability is low, but the D-dimer result is positive. Renal function is normal and she has no contrast allergy. What is the appropriate next diagnostic step?
o: Obtain computed tomographic pulmonary angiography to evaluate for embolism
End the evaluation if a chest radiograph shows no pulmonary infiltrate
Accept the positive D-dimer as confirmation of pulmonary embolism
End the evaluation on the basis of low clinical probability
explanation:
With a low clinical probability but a D-dimer above the applicable diagnostic threshold, **obtain CT pulmonary angiography** when renal function and contrast tolerance permit.

**A. CT pulmonary angiography.** This assesses the pulmonary arteries for a filling defect.
**B. Normal chest radiograph.** A normal film cannot exclude PE. It may help identify competing diagnoses.
**C. Positive D-dimer confirms PE.** D-dimer is nonspecific and can be elevated with aging, inflammation, malignancy or recent surgery.
**D. End because probability is low.** A low probability plus a negative appropriate D-dimer can exclude PE. The stated result is positive.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 96, p. 1519.

q: An older adult receiving chemotherapy for cancer has nausea. In addition to drug treatment, which dietary adjustment is described in Hazzard?
o: Large, widely spaced meals with foods that are high in fat
Large, widely spaced meals with beverages that are served hot
Small, frequent portions of food with clear, cool beverages
Small, frequent food portions with foods that are high in fat
explanation:
During chemotherapy-related nausea, small amounts may be easier to tolerate than a full meal. **Offer small, frequent portions and clear, cool drinks** alongside antiemetic treatment.

**A. Large high-fat meals.** Large portions and fatty foods are harder to tolerate during nausea.
**B. Large meals and hot drinks.** Smaller portions and cooler beverages are more consistent with reducing meal-associated symptoms.
**C. Small portions and cool drinks.** This pattern permits gradual intake of food and fluid.
**D. Small portions and high-fat foods.** Portion size fits, but lower-fat foods are generally easier to digest.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1391.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?
o: Center the evaluation on heart failure severity and the current diuretic regimen.
Center the evaluation on food intake and the need for nutritional supplements.
Assess medical, cognitive, functional, and social needs and home safety.
Center the evaluation on dementia severity and the current donepezil regimen.
explanation:
Comprehensive geriatric assessment looks across disease, cognition, function, mood, living circumstances and environment. **Assess all these domains, including home safety**, after her fall, weight loss and change of residence.

**A. Heart failure alone.** Diuretics may contribute but cannot explain medication reminders or home support.
**B. Nutrition alone.** Supplements may help, but clarify cognition, function and access to meals.
**C. Multidomain assessment.** Identify interacting causes and agree on a plan with the patient and daughter.
**D. Dementia alone.** A cognitive score does not measure nutritional, cardiac or environmental needs.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 117.
ref: Hazzard Ch 8 — PRINCIPLES OF GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT

q: A 78-year-old man with COPD, coronary artery disease, and chronic pain from lumbar spinal stenosis has increasing dyspnea that limits him to climbing one flight of stairs. He takes formoterol/budesonide, tiotropium, aspirin, metoprolol, and oxycodone 5 mg four times daily. Spirometry is unchanged from baseline, with FEV1 35% predicted. His MRC dyspnea score is 3/5 and cardiac evaluation is negative. Which statement should guide referral for pulmonary rehabilitation?
o: Defer referral because severe airflow limitation reduces the expected rehabilitation benefit.
Offer referral because symptoms persist despite pharmacologic treatment of the COPD.
Defer referral because age above seventy reduces the expected rehabilitation benefit.
Defer referral because coexisting chronic diseases reduce the expected rehabilitation benefit.
explanation:
Pulmonary rehabilitation improves exercise tolerance, skills and symptom management even when airflow obstruction persists. **Refer for rehabilitation because dyspnea limits activity despite optimized COPD treatment**.

**A. Defer for severe airflow limitation.** Patients with low FEV1 can still improve conditioning and function.
**B. Refer for persistent symptoms.** His exertional limitation is a direct rehabilitation target.
**C. Defer above age 70.** Age alone does not predict inability to benefit.
**D. Defer for comorbidity.** Adapt rehabilitation for spinal pain and cardiac history rather than automatically excluding him.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1258.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: An 83-year-old man with dementia develops delirium after starting quetiapine. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites, but there are no local urinary symptoms. He is stable and poses no danger to himself or staff. Which approach follows the source’s initial evaluation of delirium?
o: Increase quetiapine before reviewing potential precipitants
Add haloperidol before reviewing potential precipitants
Investigate precipitants and review the newly prescribed drug
Use urine results to replace the review of other precipitants
explanation:
Delirium may have more than one precipitant. Pyuria and nitrites without urinary symptoms in a stable older person cannot identify a symptomatic urinary infection by themselves.
**Evaluate the acute change broadly, including the recently started quetiapine and its indication.**

**A. Increase quetiapine before reviewing potential precipitants.** Increasing a new centrally active drug before assessing adverse effects can intensify sedation or confusion.
**B. Add haloperidol before reviewing potential precipitants.** Adding a second antipsychotic without a dangerous behavior indication increases risk.
**C. Investigate precipitants and review the newly prescribed drug.** The timing suggests a medication contribution worth addressing along with other medical causes.
**D. Use urine results to replace the review of other precipitants.** Urine findings alone do not explain this syndrome or replace the drug review.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–885, 889. IDSA asymptomatic bacteriuria guideline 2019, recommendation V.1

q: An 86-year-old man is readmitted with advanced lung disease. He is receiving treatment for an exacerbation but has severe symptoms and unclear goals of care. He is alert and wants to understand his options. When is palliative care consultation appropriate?
o: After a hospice decision and discontinuation of disease treatment
After further deterioration identifies the final days of life
During this admission for symptom relief and goal clarification
At discharge planning after the current exacerbation has been treated
explanation:
Palliative care can relieve symptoms and help patients make complex decisions throughout serious illness. **Consult during this admission** because symptoms are severe and the patient wants to understand his options.

**A. After hospice election.** Palliative care does not require hospice or withdrawal of treatment.
**B. Only in the final days.** Waiting would prolong distress and delay decisions.
**C. During the admission.** The team can address symptoms alongside treatment of the exacerbation.
**D. At discharge only.** Current symptom burden and questions already warrant action.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1082.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1052, 1082, Figure 70-3

q: A 79-year-old woman with mild dementia develops an acute change in attention and awareness. She takes diphenhydramine and has hyponatremia. Urinalysis shows pyuria, but an infectious source has not been established. How should the evaluation proceed?
o: Focus the etiologic evaluation on urine findings and complete an infection workup
Focus the etiologic evaluation on sodium and complete an electrolyte workup
Evaluate medications, metabolic disorders, and acute illnesses during the workup
Focus the etiologic evaluation on dementia and complete a cognitive assessment
explanation:
A vulnerable patient can develop delirium from several modest insults. Anticholinergic exposure and hyponatremia are specific clues, while pyuria alone does not diagnose symptomatic infection.
**Evaluate the diphenhydramine, sodium disturbance and possible acute illnesses together.**

**A. Focus the etiologic evaluation on urine findings and complete an infection workup.** Investigating urine alone leaves two recognized, potentially treatable contributors unaddressed.
**B. Focus the etiologic evaluation on sodium and complete an electrolyte workup.** Correcting sodium is important but does not eliminate the need to assess exposures and infection.
**C. Evaluate medications, metabolic disorders, and acute illnesses during the workup.** A comprehensive, clinically directed workup follows the multifactorial pattern.
**D. Focus the etiologic evaluation on dementia and complete a cognitive assessment.** Baseline dementia increases vulnerability and cannot account by itself for the new change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 881–883, 885. IDSA asymptomatic bacteriuria guideline 2019, recommendation V.1

q: An 84-year-old man with frailty (four of five Fried criteria), heart failure, and moderate CKD (Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 35 mL/min) lives at home with a 24-hour caregiver. He has monthly heart-failure admissions despite optimized medication. A cardiologist recommends a primary-prevention ICD. The patient is hesitant, while his son, who holds medical power of attorney, strongly favors implantation. Before deciding about the device, which clinical approach best matches Hazzard?
o: Proceed with implantation on the basis of the son's expressed preference
Decline implantation on the basis of the frailty assessment alone
Discuss goals with the patient and family, with palliative-care input
Seek formal ethics mediation before exploring the patient's treatment goals
explanation:
A primary-prevention ICD reduces arrhythmic death but cannot treat every cause of mortality or recurrent hospitalization. **Discuss goals, competing illness and life expectancy with the patient and family, including palliative input**.

**A. Proceed on the son's preference.** Medical power of attorney does not displace the patient's voice when he can participate.
**B. Decline on frailty alone.** Frailty informs prognosis without settling individual benefit.
**C. Shared discussion.** Explore potential shocks, survival benefit, treatment burdens and his priorities.
**D. Ethics mediation first.** An ordinary goals discussion can begin before any need for formal dispute resolution.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1184, 1047.

q: אישה בישראל המטופלת בדיאליזה מחזורית הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. היא בעלת כשרות, מבינה את משמעות ההחלטה ומסרבת לחידוש הדיאליזה כדי שלא להאריך את חייה. מחזור הטיפול הקודם הסתיים. מהו העיקרון החל לפי החוק?
o: להמשיך במחזור הבא עד לקבלת הסכמת משפחתה
להמשיך במחזור הבא עד להחלטת ועדה מוסדית
להמשיך במחזור הבא בשל עצם תלותה בדיאליזה
לכבד את סירובה לחידוש הטיפול המחזורי
explanation:
דיאליזה ניתנת במחזורים נפרדים. כשהחולה הכשירה שעליה חל החוק מסרבת מדעת להתחלת מחזור חדש, ההחלטה נוגעת לאי־חידוש. **לכבד את סירובה לחידוש הטיפול המחזורי**.

**א. להמשיך במחזור הבא עד לקבלת הסכמת משפחתה.** אישור המשפחה אינו תנאי לבחירתה המודעת.
**ב. להמשיך במחזור הבא עד להחלטת ועדה מוסדית.** החלטה של ועדה אינה נדרשת לכל סירוב ברור.
**ג. להמשיך במחזור הבא בשל עצם תלותה בדיאליזה.** התלות הרפואית בדיאליזה מסבירה את הסיכון שיש להציג.
**ד. לכבד את סירובה לחידוש הטיפול המחזורי.** המחזור הקודם הסתיים ולכן ניתן לכבד את הסירוב לחידוש.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו־2005, עמ׳ 10, 12.

q: An 81-year-old man has fallen twice at night and reports insomnia. A falls assessment has been completed. He takes no sleep medication and has no sedative dependence. Which initial sleep approach is consistent with reducing exposure to medications implicated in falls?
o: Begin a short-acting benzodiazepine for insomnia.
Begin a nonpharmacologic intervention for insomnia.
Begin a Z-drug hypnotic for insomnia.
Begin a sedating psychotropic medication for insomnia.
explanation:
A new insomnia treatment should account for this man's nighttime falls and lack of an existing sedative dependence. **Begin a behavioral or other nonpharmacologic intervention** to avoid adding psychomotor impairment.

**A. Short-acting benzodiazepine.** Short duration does not eliminate sedation or falls during nighttime activity.
**B. Nonpharmacologic intervention.** Addresses insomnia while keeping him free of a new fall-risk medication.
**C. Z-drug.** Nonbenzodiazepine hypnotics can still cause impaired balance and fall-related injuries.
**D. Sedating psychotropic.** Increasing central sedation can make an already hazardous nighttime trip less safe.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 639.

q: אישה בת 92 עם דמנציה קשה (MMSE 8/30) בבית אבות לא אכלה במשך 5 ימים ואיבדה 15% ממשקל גופה במשך 3 חודשים. היא קופצת את פיה כאשר מציעים לה אוכל ודוחה כלי אוכל. הערכת בליעה אינה מראה ליקוי מכני. בתה מבקשת הכנסת צינור הזנה ואומרת: "אני לא יכולה לתת לאמי לגווע ברעב." כיצד צריך הצוות הפליאטיבי להגיב?
o: להמליץ על הכנסת PEG כצעד הבא בתגובה לבקשת הבת להזין את אמה
להמליץ על הימנעות מהזנה מלאכותית כצעד הבא בשל אבחנת הדמנציה הקשה
להמליץ על ניסיון בזונדה כצעד הבא לפני בירור הסיבה לסירוב לאכול
להמליץ על הערכה רב־מקצועית כצעד הבא לבירור הסירוב ובחירת דרך ההזנה
explanation:
ירידה באכילה בדמנציה יכולה לנבוע מכאב, בעיית בליעה, מחלה חריפה או קושי בסיוע. מבררים את מצבה ומכירים בדאגת הבת לפני בחירת דרך ההזנה. **להמליץ על הערכה רב־מקצועית כצעד הבא לבירור הסירוב ובחירת דרך ההזנה**.

**א. להמליץ על הכנסת PEG כצעד הבא בתגובה לבקשת הבת להזין את אמה.** בקשת הבת מבטאת חשש חשוב אך אינה קובעת התוויה ל־PEG.
**ב. להמליץ על הימנעות מהזנה מלאכותית כצעד הבא בשל אבחנת הדמנציה הקשה.** אבחנת דמנציה לבדה אינה קובעת את דרך ההזנה.
**ג. להמליץ על ניסיון בזונדה כצעד הבא לפני בירור הסיבה לסירוב לאכול.** זונדה היא אפשרות שיש לשקול לאחר בירור התועלת והסיכון.
**ד. להמליץ על הערכה רב־מקצועית כצעד הבא לבירור הסירוב ובחירת דרך ההזנה.** הצוות מעריך תזונה, בליעה ואפשרות לסיוע ומציג למשפחה חלופות מתאימות.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית בעניין הזנה לחולה עם קיהיון, עמ׳ 5 עד 6.
ref: MoH National Committee PEG recommendations · pp. 4–6; decisions ד–ט
label: Source: MoH National Committee PEG recommendations · pp. 4–6; decisions ד–ט

q: A 78-year-old man receiving morphine develops worsening renal function, somnolence, and myoclonus. Which medication-related mechanism should raise concern?
o: Declining renal function with increased metabolite clearance
Improving renal function with increased metabolite accumulation
Declining renal function with accumulation of metabolites
Improving renal function with accelerated metabolite elimination
explanation:
Declining renal function can increase exposure to morphine metabolites. **Metabolite accumulation is a plausible explanation for new somnolence and myoclonus**.

**A. Declining function with faster clearance.** Worsening filtration usually slows elimination.
**B. Improving function with accumulation.** Improved filtration would generally favor elimination.
**C. Declining function with accumulation.** The neurologic findings should prompt immediate review of morphine exposure and other causes.
**D. Improving function and faster elimination.** This does not fit the renal trajectory or new symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: Intermittent catheterization is being considered for a woman with urinary retention. Which management principle follows Hazzard?
o: Adjust the frequency according to measured residual urine volumes
Choose an indwelling catheter because it has fewer management risks
Lengthen catheterization intervals to allow higher residual urine volumes
Require a sterile catheter technique if treatment continues at home
explanation:
Intermittent catheterization periodically empties a bladder that cannot empty adequately on its own. **Adjust frequency to measured residual volumes** so the bladder does not become repeatedly overdistended.

**A. Use residuals to set frequency.** More retained urine may require shorter intervals. Reassess as bladder function changes.
**B. Prefer an indwelling catheter for lower risk.** Long-term indwelling catheters carry substantial infection and other management risks.
**C. Lengthen intervals to increase residuals.** The aim is to avoid large retained volumes, not deliberately permit them.
**D. Require sterile technique at home.** Clean intermittent technique is generally appropriate at home with proper instruction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 715.

q: A 76-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen, heart failure (EF 25%), and stage 3b CKD has worsening dyspnea over several months despite optimized disease-directed treatment. He is homebound and uses a walker for short distances. His wife provides round-the-clock care and appears exhausted. He asks about hospice but says, “I am not ready to give up.” Which response best explains an available approach?
o: Provide home palliative care alongside ongoing treatment of his illnesses
Palliative care should follow withdrawal of disease-directed treatment
Palliative care referral should await a prognosis shorter than six months
Symptom management should be completed before discussing care goals
explanation:
Home palliative care can address refractory symptoms, family caregiving strain and future decisions in serious illness. **Offer it alongside ongoing heart-failure and COPD treatment**.

**A. Home palliative care.** It can address breathlessness and his wife's exhaustion without requiring abandonment of treatment.
**B. Only after withdrawal.** Palliative and disease-directed care can coexist.
**C. Wait for short prognosis.** Palliative referral does not require the Medicare hospice prognosis threshold.
**D. Control symptoms before goals.** Goals discussions can guide symptom treatment and caregiver support now.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1084, 1046.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: מטופל נקבע כחולה הנוטה למות ואינו בעל כשרות. נשקלות החלטות לפי החוק, ונמסר שבעבר הביע רצונות בנוגע לטיפול. מה נדרש מהרופא האחראי בבירור רצונו?
o: להסתפק בדרישת האחיין הנוכחית ולהתחיל לפעול לפיה
להסתפק בהתרשמות הצוות ולוותר על בירור מסמכים קודמים
לברר הנחיות וייפוי כוח ולאסוף תיעוד רלוונטי
להסיק מחוסר יכולתו לדבר שלא הביע העדפות טיפול בעבר
explanation:
כשחולה שאינו יכול להתבטא זקוק להחלטה, מחפשים מה ביקש כשהיה יכול להחליט. אין להניח ששתיקתו בהווה מעידה על עמדתו. **לברר הנחיות וייפוי כוח ולאסוף תיעוד רלוונטי**.

**א. להסתפק בדרישת האחיין הנוכחית ולהתחיל לפעול לפיה.** האחיין יכול למסור מידע אך דרישתו אינה מכריעה.
**ב. להסתפק בהתרשמות הצוות ולוותר על בירור מסמכים קודמים.** התרשמות הצוות אינה תחליף לחיפוש מידע על רצונו.
**ג. לברר הנחיות וייפוי כוח ולאסוף תיעוד רלוונטי.** בודקים מסמכים, רישומים והצהרות רלוונטיות.
**ד. להסיק מחוסר יכולתו לדבר שלא הביע העדפות טיפול בעבר.** קושי בדיבור כעת אינו שולל קיומן של העדפות קודמות.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 9, עמ׳ 7.
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A 79-year-old woman with advanced heart failure asks about life expectancy so that she can plan. Her physician has a prognostic estimate but substantial uncertainty remains for the individual. How should it be communicated?
o: Present the group mean as her personal survival date for planning
Postpone prognostic details until an exact survival date can be given
Present a range or scenarios and explain the uncertainty
Focus on symptoms to reduce the need to discuss expected survival
explanation:
Prognostic estimates describe likely courses in groups and remain uncertain for an individual. **Give a range or plausible scenarios and explain the uncertainty** to help her plan.

**A. Personal survival date from a mean.** A group average cannot predict her exact date.
**B. Wait for certainty.** Exact prediction is usually impossible and delay limits planning.
**C. Range or scenarios.** Typical, better and worse courses give practical context without false precision.
**D. Discuss symptoms alone.** She explicitly asked for a survival estimate to guide decisions.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A patient near the end of life has severe agitated delirium. After an appropriate evaluation and initial treatment, sedation is agreed with the family to be consistent with the goals of care. Which drug characteristic is recommended?
o: Long duration of action with titration to the clinical effect
Short duration of action with titration to effect
Long duration of action with a predetermined fixed dose
Short duration of action with a predetermined fixed dose
explanation:
Palliative sedation is a symptom-directed intervention for severe refractory distress. Choose an agent and dose that allow adjustment of the balance between comfort, breathing and communication.
**Use a short-acting agent titrated to the relief required.**

**A. Long duration of action with titration to the clinical effect.** Titration is appropriate but a long duration makes the effect less adjustable.
**B. Short duration of action with titration to effect.** Short action and titration help preserve as much interaction as the comfort goal allows.
**C. Long duration of action with a predetermined fixed dose.** A fixed long-acting dose is difficult to adjust if distress or sedation changes.
**D. Short duration of action with a predetermined fixed dose.** Short action helps, but a predetermined dose ignores the individual response.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 890

q: An 85-year-old woman with severe COPD (FEV1 22%), osteoporosis, and severe frailty (CFS 7) lives alone with daily home help. She is hospitalized with influenza and respiratory failure requiring BiPAP. After recovery, she wants to return home and understands the risks, although the team is concerned about safety. Which plan combines her goal with the source approach to advanced COPD and diminished abilities?
o: Return home with prior services and defer reassessment of support needs
Move to residential care and defer discussion of her preference for home
Return home and discontinue COPD treatments when palliative care begins
Return home with palliative care and support matched to her needs
explanation:
Palliative care for advanced COPD can preserve independence through symptom relief and practical support. **Plan a return home with services matched to her assessed needs and preferences**.

**A. Resume previous services unchanged.** Severe frailty and a new admission warrant reassessing what help is sufficient.
**B. Residential care without discussing home.** Her informed preference should shape planning.
**C. Stop COPD treatment.** Therapies that improve breathlessness or prevent exacerbations can continue.
**D. Adapt home support.** Address mobility, supervision, caregiver availability and symptom management.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1049, 1262.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: גבר בן 77 לאחר ניתוח ודליריום שחלף משתתף בתכנון השיקום. הוא מבין את האפשרויות ואת השלכותיהן ומביע העדפה עקבית. מהו עיקרון שיתופו לפי חוזר משרד הבריאות על שיקום לקשישים?
o: לסכם תוכנית בצוות ולהציג למטופל את המסגרת שנבחרה
למסור מידע ולשתפו בהסכמה לכל מרכיבי התהליך
לסכם תוכנית עם המשפחה ולהציג למטופל את מועד המעבר
למסור מידע על העלויות ולבחור מסגרת לפי כיסוי המבטח
explanation:
**יש למסור למטופל מידע ולשתפו בהסכמה לכל מרכיבי השיקום.** לאחר שהדליריום חלף הוא מבין את האפשרויות ומסוגל להביע העדפה.

**א. החלטת צוות לפני השיחה.** הצגת החלטה מוגמרת מגבילה שותפות בבחירה.
**ב. מידע והסכמה לכל מרכיב.** משווים מטרות, עצימות, מסגרת וחלופות בהתאם לצרכיו ולהעדפותיו.
**ג. קביעה בידי המשפחה.** תמיכה משפחתית מועילה, אך אינה מחליפה את המטופל הכשיר.
**ד. עלות וכיסוי בלבד.** הכיסוי הוא אילוץ מעשי לצד ההתאמה הקלינית והבחירה המושכלת.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר מינהל רפואה 4/2009, סעיף 5.4.

q: An 80-year-old woman with advanced heart failure, moderate dementia, and pressure ulcers has lived in a nursing home for eight months. Monthly admissions for fluid overload are followed by functional decline. She cries during transfers and refuses physical therapy. Her son demands every treatment but has not visited for months. Which intervention directly addresses the need to clarify goals and align the care plan?
o: Increase the loop diuretic dose to reduce congestion
Arrange family meetings to clarify goals and care
Start antidepressant treatment for the reported emotional distress
Arrange transfer to a facility providing a higher level of care
explanation:
A family meeting brings the patient, surrogate and care team together to discuss disease trajectory and goals. **Arrange a meeting to clarify what treatment should achieve** during recurrent admissions and decline.

**A. Increase diuretics.** This may relieve congestion but does not resolve disagreement about care.
**B. Family meeting.** Discuss the patient's wishes, observed distress and realistic outcomes with her son.
**C. Start an antidepressant.** Crying during transfers may reflect pain or fear and does not itself diagnose depression.
**D. Move facilities.** A different care site cannot substitute for clarifying goals.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1082, 1182.
ref: Hazzard Ch 70 — PALLIATIVE CARE ACROSS CARE SETTINGS

q: גבר בן 85 עם פרקינסון מתקדם בשלב 4 לפי H&Y ודמנציה מתונה מאושפז מבית אבות עם דלקת ריאות משאיפה. בתו, המחזיקה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, נפגשת איתך לדון במטרות הטיפול. היא אומרת: "הוא אמר לי שמעולם לא רצה להישאר בחיים על מכונות, אבל אני לא יכולה לתת לו למות. האם נוכל פשוט לנסות את המכונה כמה ימים?" התרופות הנוכחיות שלו כוללות carbidopa-levodopa, donepezil ו-quetiapine 50 mg QHS. סימנים חיוניים: T 38.5°C, HR 110, BP 95/60, RR 28, SpO2 88% על 6L O2. מהי התגובה הראשונית המתאימה ביותר?
o: אני מבין את הקושי. נקבל את דבריו הקודמים כהחלטה להימנע מהנשמה ונעבור כעת לטיפול ממוקד נוחות בלי בירור נוסף.
אני מבין את הקושי. נדבר על משמעות הניסיון לכמה ימים ועל מה שנקווה להשיג, ונברר כיצד הבקשה מתיישבת עם רצונו.
אני מבין את הקושי. בגלל הדמנציה דבריו הקודמים איבדו תוקף, ולכן נבקש ממך לקבל במקומו את ההחלטה לגבי ההנשמה.
אני מבין את הקושי. נתחיל בהנשמה באמצעות צינור כעת ונעריך את מצבו מחדש בתוך 72 שעות, לפי התגובה לטיפול.
explanation:
כשמשפחה שוקלת ניסיון טיפולי מוגבל בזמן, מבררים את רצונו הקודם של המטופל, את הסיכוי לשיפור ואת אמות המידה להמשך או לשינוי. במקביל מטפלים במצוקה הנשימתית. **אני מבין את הקושי. נדבר על משמעות הניסיון לכמה ימים ועל מה שנקווה להשיג, ונברר כיצד הבקשה מתיישבת עם רצונו**.

**א. אני מבין את הקושי. נקבל את דבריו הקודמים כהחלטה להימנע מהנשמה ונעבור כעת לטיפול ממוקד נוחות בלי בירור נוסף.** אמירה קודמת דורשת הבנת ההקשר והאם היא מתייחסת להתערבות המסוימת.
**ב. אני מבין את הקושי. נדבר על משמעות הניסיון לכמה ימים ועל מה שנקווה להשיג, ונברר כיצד הבקשה מתיישבת עם רצונו.** מגדירים עם המשפחה את מטרת הניסיון, משכו ומה ייחשב שיפור מבחינת המטופל.
**ג. אני מבין את הקושי. בגלל הדמנציה דבריו הקודמים איבדו תוקף, ולכן נבקש ממך לקבל במקומו את ההחלטה לגבי ההנשמה.** דמנציה אינה מבטלת אוטומטית העדפות קודמות.
**ד. אני מבין את הקושי. נתחיל בהנשמה באמצעות צינור כעת ונעריך את מצבו מחדש בתוך 72 שעות, לפי התגובה לטיפול.** אין להתחייב להנשמה פולשנית בלי לברר מידת דחיפות, רצון והצדקה קלינית.

אסמכתא · משרד המשפטים, מדריך לייפוי כוח מתמשך, עמ׳ 5; חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8.
ref: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך

q: A woman with advanced illness requests a survival estimate to plan her affairs. When a clinical estimate is available, how does Hazzard recommend communicating it?
o: Provide a precise date and narrow the discussion of possible outcomes
Provide a range and acknowledge uncertainty in the estimate
Emphasize an optimistic point estimate when describing expected survival
Provide a numerical estimate and set aside the emotional response
explanation:
Communicating prognosis should support planning and allow an emotional response. **Offer a range and acknowledge uncertainty** when an estimate is available and desired.

**A. Give a precise date.** Individual survival varies even with similar disease severity.
**B. Range with uncertainty.** Describe the likely course and what could make it shorter or longer.
**C. Optimistic point estimate.** It may distort decisions and omit plausible less favorable outcomes.
**D. Ignore emotion.** Understanding and emotional support matter as much as the number.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 81-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18) presents after a fall. His daughter reports more confusion and frequent falls. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, and trazodone 100 mg nightly, started two weeks ago for sleep. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. Which action directly removes the newly introduced drug associated in Hazzard with daytime sleepiness and orthostatic hypotension?
o: Discontinue donepezil while continuing the recently introduced trazodone.
Discontinue trazodone as a possible contributor to the symptoms.
Reduce amlodipine while continuing the recently introduced trazodone.
Add fludrocortisone while continuing the recently introduced trazodone.
explanation:
New trazodone can cause daytime sleepiness and orthostatic hypotension. With more falls and a 30 mmHg standing systolic drop after starting it, **withdraw trazodone as a possible contributor and reassess**.

**A. Stop donepezil alone.** Other drugs may warrant review, but this leaves the newly introduced sedative unchanged.
**B. Stop trazodone.** The timing and adverse-effect profile make supervised withdrawal a direct way to reduce exposure.
**C. Reduce amlodipine alone.** Blood pressure therapy may also matter, but the recently added sleep drug would remain.
**D. Add fludrocortisone first.** Treating the adverse effect with another drug before reviewing its cause can increase treatment burden.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 121, 661.

q: בת 92 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. משפחתה מבקשת PEG בגלל שאיפות חוזרות. מה מתואר בסיכום המחקרים במסמך הוועדה הארצית, לצד ההסתייגות ממגבלותיהם?
o: שיעורי שאיפה דומים בין דרכי ההזנה שנבדקו
שיעור שאיפה מופחת עם PEG בהשוואה להזנה פומית
שיעור שאיפה מופחת עם זונדה בהשוואה להזנה פומית
שיעור שאיפה מופחת עם עירוי בהשוואה להזנה פומית
explanation:
**לא הודגם יתרון עקבי של צינור הזנה במניעת אספירציות** בהשוואות שסקרה הוועדה בדמנציה מתקדמת. גם רוק ותוכן קיבה יכולים להישאף.

**א. שיעורי שאיפה דומים.** כך תוארו ההשוואות, תוך הסתייגות מהטיות ומהבדלים בין אוכלוסיות המחקר.
**ב. PEG מפחית שאיפה.** הוא עוקף חלק ממסלול הבליעה אך אינו מונע כל שאיפה.
**ג. זונדה מפחיתה שאיפה.** הימצאות צינור אינה מבטיחה הגנה על דרכי הנשימה.
**ד. עירוי מפחית שאיפה.** הנתונים אינם מצדיקים המלצה על הזנה תוך־ורידית למניעת אספירציה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, המלצות המותב על PEG בחולה עם קיהיון הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 4–5.
ref: משרד הבריאות, המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות: PEG לחולה עם קיהיון שהוא נוטה למות

q: An 84-year-old man with heart failure and impaired renal function takes spironolactone. Creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL and potassium 5.3 mEq/L. Which adjustment matches the contraindications in Hazzard's heart-failure chapter?
o: Continue spironolactone and monitor potassium and renal function
Stop spironolactone and monitor potassium and renal function
Switch to eplerenone and monitor potassium and renal function
Increase spironolactone and monitor potassium and renal function
explanation:
With creatinine 2.8 mg/dL and elevated potassium, **stop spironolactone and reassess renal function and potassium**. The combination puts this patient at high risk of further hyperkalemia.

**A. Continue without adjusting.** Monitoring alone leaves the offending potassium-sparing drug in place.
**B. Stop and monitor.** The chapter identifies substantial renal dysfunction and preexisting hyperkalemia as safety concerns.
**C. Switch to eplerenone.** Its greater receptor selectivity does not remove its potassium-retaining effect.
**D. Increase spironolactone.** A higher dose would aggravate the risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 76, p. 1181.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.1181

q: A 79-year-old woman with dementia becomes acutely confused after starting oxybutynin. She is stable, with no fever, dysuria, flank pain, or new urinary symptom. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites. She has no catheter, focal neurologic deficit, or immediately dangerous behavior. Which approach is appropriate now?
o: Continue oxybutynin and start antibiotics on the basis of the urinalysis
Stop oxybutynin and investigate delirium contributors while monitoring
Continue oxybutynin and start an antipsychotic for the acute confusion
Stop oxybutynin and start antibiotics on the basis of the urinalysis
explanation:
Oxybutynin can impair cognition through muscarinic blockade. Pyuria or nitrites without local symptoms or systemic illness do not justify attributing delirium to urinary infection.
**Stop the unnecessary new oxybutynin, investigate other contributors and observe clinically.**

**A. Continue oxybutynin and start antibiotics on the basis of the urinalysis.** This retains a plausible drug precipitant and adds antibiotics without a symptomatic indication.
**B. Stop oxybutynin and investigate delirium contributors while monitoring.** Withdrawal addresses the timing and mechanism while monitoring permits reassessment if urinary or systemic signs develop.
**C. Continue oxybutynin and start an antipsychotic for the acute confusion.** An antipsychotic does not remove the new anticholinergic exposure and she poses no immediate danger.
**D. Stop oxybutynin and start antibiotics on the basis of the urinalysis.** Stopping oxybutynin is appropriate. The urine result alone is insufficient reason for antibiotics.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–885. AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Table 7, p. 2074. IDSA asymptomatic bacteriuria guideline 2019, recommendation V.1

q: מטופל מבוגר המסוגל לקבל החלטות מבקש להשוות בין החייאה עתידית לבין חלופותיה. כבר הוסברו לו האבחנה, הפרוגנוזה ומהות פעולות ההחייאה. איזה מידע נוסף נותן מענה לחובת ההסבר על הטיפול ועל החלופות לפי סעיף 13(ב) לחוק זכויות החולה?
o: פירוט התועלת והסיכונים בהחייאה ובחלופותיה, לרבות האפשרות להימנע מטיפול
פירוט זמני ההחייאה, שלבי הביצוע והציוד הדרוש בחדר הטיפולים
פירוט העדפות המשפחה, עמדות קרוביו וההמלצה המשותפת שלהם לטיפול
פירוט הפרוגנוזה, מחלות הרקע והשפעתן הצפויה על התקדמות השיקום
explanation:
**יש להסביר את התועלת והסיכונים של החייאה ושל החלופות, לרבות הימנעות מהחייאה.** המידע צריך להיות מובן ורלוונטי למצב האדם ולמטרותיו.

**א. תועלת וסיכונים בכל חלופה.** מאפשרים לבחור בין אפשרויות ממשיות לאחר הבנת התוצאות הצפויות.
**ב. טכניקה וציוד.** מידע טכני אינו נותן מענה לשאלת התועלת, הנזק והחלופות.
**ג. העדפות המשפחה.** אפשר לשתפן בהסכמת המטופל, אך הבחירה שלו.
**ד. הפרוגנוזה והתחלואה בלבד.** חלק חשוב מהרקע, אך חסר הסבר על ההחייאה מול הימנעות ממנה.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13(ב).
ref: Hazzard Ch 7 — DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: אישה בת 77 עם סרטן ודליריום נבדקה בזמן צלילות ונמצאה מסוגלת לקבל את ההחלטה הטיפולית הנדונה. אין מצב חירום. ילדיה חלוקים לגבי הטיפול, והיא מבקשת הסבר כדי להחליט. מה צריך להנחות את השיחה?
o: הצגת עמדת הילדה התומכת בטיפול והחתמתה על הסכמה
מסירת מידע מובן למטופלת כדי לאפשר בחירה רצונית
הצגת עמדת הילד התומך בנוחות והחתמתו על הסכמה
העברת בחירת הטיפול לצוות בגלל חילוקי הדעות במשפחה
explanation:
המטופלת יכולה לבחור בין טיפול מכוון מחלה לבין טיפול ממוקד הקלה לאחר הסבר נגיש על התועלת והמחיר של כל דרך. **מסירת מידע מובן למטופלת כדי לאפשר בחירה רצונית**.

**א. הצגת עמדת הילדה התומכת בטיפול והחתמתה על הסכמה.** תמיכת הבת בטיפול אינה מקנה לה סמכות להסכים במקום אמה.
**ב. מסירת מידע מובן למטופלת כדי לאפשר בחירה רצונית.** מבררים מה חשוב למטופלת ומאפשרים לה לבחור מרצונה.
**ג. הצגת עמדת הילד התומך בנוחות והחתמתו על הסכמה.** גם העדפת הבן לנוחות אינה מחליפה את בחירתה.
**ד. העברת בחירת הטיפול לצוות בגלל חילוקי הדעות במשפחה.** חילוקי דעות במשפחה אינם שוללים את כשרות המטופלת.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8.

q: An 82-year-old man with falls has taken lorazepam every night for two years. Which consideration supports reviewing the treatment with attention to physical dependence, according to Beers 2023?
o: Continued use is associated with reduced sensitivity and fewer falls
Continued use is associated with physical dependence and increased falls
Continued use is associated with reduced dependence and improved stability
Continued use is associated with improved cognition and reduced dependence
explanation:
Regular benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence. Sedation and impaired coordination can continue to increase fall risk during long-term treatment.

**Consider both dependence and fall risk when reviewing nightly lorazepam.** After two years of use, assess withdrawal risk and plan any reduction gradually.

**A. Less sensitivity and fewer falls.** Older adults are more sensitive to benzodiazepines, and continued use offers no protection against falls.
**B. Dependence and more falls.** Both problems matter when balancing continued treatment against a supervised reduction.
**C. Less dependence and better stability.** Long-term exposure can increase dependence and impair balance.
**D. Better cognition and less dependence.** Benzodiazepines can impair cognition and lead to physical dependence during continued use.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2060.

q: A woman with COPD remains breathless at rest despite optimal treatment of her lung disease. Which principle applies to drug treatment of refractory dyspnea according to Hazzard?
o: Consider replacing lung-disease treatment with an opioid for symptom relief
Consider selecting an opioid without accounting for cognitive changes
Consider an opioid for symptom relief while monitoring adverse effects
Consider selecting morphine without accounting for impaired kidney function
explanation:
Refractory dyspnea persists despite appropriate treatment of the underlying illness. **An individualized opioid trial may relieve symptoms, with monitoring for cognitive and other adverse effects**.

**A. Replace COPD treatment.** Continue beneficial cause-directed care while adding symptom relief.
**B. Ignore cognition.** Sedation or confusion may outweigh relief for the individual.
**C. Monitor a symptom trial.** Assess perceived breathlessness, alertness and tolerability.
**D. Ignore kidney impairment.** Morphine metabolites can accumulate, altering the choice or dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: A woman with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction has pulmonary congestion and is receiving a diuretic. Which principle should guide adjustment of treatment intensity?
o: Increase diuresis until relative hypotension develops
Relieve congestion while avoiding excessive diuresis
Reduce diuresis in order to maintain pulmonary congestion
Titrate diuresis to produce a fall in cardiac output
explanation:
In HFpEF, **relieve congestion while avoiding excessive diuresis**. A stiff ventricle may depend on adequate filling pressure to maintain stroke volume.

**A. Diurese until hypotension.** Symptomatic hypotension suggests excessive volume reduction or poor perfusion.
**B. Relieve congestion cautiously.** Use symptoms, examination, weight, renal function and electrolytes to guide adjustments.
**C. Maintain pulmonary congestion.** Leaving excess filling pressure untreated perpetuates dyspnea.
**D. Aim for lower cardiac output.** Reduced forward flow is a potential complication, not a therapeutic target.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 76, p. 1186.

q: A 91-year-old man with Parkinson disease, falls, and orthostatic hypotension takes amitriptyline for pain. The team has decided to remove an antidepressant with strong anticholinergic activity. Which plan accomplishes this under Beers 2023?
o: Replace amitriptyline with imipramine for continued pain management
Discontinue amitriptyline and plan an alternative pain treatment
Replace amitriptyline with clomipramine for continued pain management
Replace amitriptyline with nortriptyline for continued pain management
explanation:
Tricyclic antidepressants used for pain can still cause sedation, anticholinergic symptoms, and orthostatic hypotension. Switching among the listed tricyclics would preserve those concerns.

**Discontinue amitriptyline and plan another way to treat pain.** This removes the targeted exposure in a man already affected by falls and orthostasis.

**A. Switch to imipramine.** Imipramine also has strong anticholinergic activity and can worsen standing symptoms.
**B. Discontinue and plan alternative analgesia.** This addresses the drug risk without overlooking the pain for which it was prescribed.
**C. Switch to clomipramine.** Clomipramine retains strong anticholinergic activity and sedation.
**D. Switch to nortriptyline.** Nortriptyline is also among the strongly anticholinergic antidepressants in older adults.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2059.

q: אישה עם ירידה קוגניטיבית קלה יכולה להבין ולקבל החלטות בנוגע לענייניה כאשר המידע מונגש לה. נשקלת קבלת החלטות נתמכת בישראל. מהו תפקיד התומך?
o: לקבל החלטות במקומה לאחר שמיעת העדפותיה
לסייע לה לבטא ולממש את החלטותיה
להעביר את ההחלטות לבת לאחר בירור רצונותיה
לבחור עבורה מסגרת מגורים בהתאם להמלצה רפואית
explanation:
תומך החלטות עוזר לאדם להבין, לבטא ולממש את רצונו. סמכות ההחלטה נשארת אצל האדם. **לסייע לה לבטא ולממש את החלטותיה**.

**א. לקבל החלטות במקומה לאחר שמיעת העדפותיה.** הקשבה להעדפה אינה מסמיכה לבחור במקומה.
**ב. לסייע לה לבטא ולממש את החלטותיה.** מנגישים מידע ומסייעים בביצוע ההחלטה שבחרה.
**ג. להעביר את ההחלטות לבת לאחר בירור רצונותיה.** הבת אינה מקבלת סמכות במקום המטופלת.
**ד. לבחור עבורה מסגרת מגורים בהתאם להמלצה רפואית.** המלצה רפואית היא מידע לשקילה, לא החלטה של התומך.

אסמכתא · חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 67ב, עמ׳ 62.
chapterTitle: COMMUNITY-BASED LONG-TERM SERVICES AND SUPPORT, AND HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE

q: An 83-year-old man with metastatic cancer and uncontrolled pain says he will harm himself if the pain continues. In addition to treating pain, what should be assessed now to evaluate suicide risk?
o: Daily function, walking ability, and support needed for transfers
Appetite, weight change, and the composition of daily meals
Memory, orientation, and ability to manage personal finances
Suicidal thoughts, intent, plans, and access to means
explanation:
A conditional threat of self-harm requires **immediate assessment of suicidal thoughts, intent, plans and access to means**, alongside prompt pain treatment. Establish whether the patient can remain safe and arrange the level of supervision indicated.

**A. Mobility and transfer needs.** Functional assessment helps discharge planning but cannot determine imminent suicide risk.
**B. Appetite and weight.** Nutritional symptoms may contribute to distress and can be assessed after immediate safety.
**C. Memory and finances.** Cognitive capacity may influence care planning but does not replace direct assessment of intent.
**D. Intent, plans and access.** These clarify immediacy and inform protective measures, clinical observation and urgent mental health involvement.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1030.
ref: Hazzard Ch 66 — GENERAL TOPICS IN GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY

q: An 80-year-old woman with heart failure, chronic kidney disease and newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. The oncologist recommends pembrolizumab, while the cardiologist is concerned about cardiac toxicity. She lives independently and manages her instrumental activities. She says, "I want to fight the cancer, but I also want to be at home with my grandchildren." What should the team clarify to align the treatment plan with her priorities?
o: The most intensive cancer treatment supported by a disease-specific protocol
The competing illness that should determine care before exploring her goals
The treatment to select from functional status before discussing her goals
Her priorities for time at home and quality of life
explanation:
Goals-of-care discussions help balance hoped-for benefit against treatment burdens. **Clarify how she values time at home and quality of life alongside cancer control** before selecting treatment.

**A. Most intensive protocol.** A protocol cannot decide which tradeoffs she would accept.
**B. Let one disease dictate care.** Both heart failure and cancer affect achievable outcomes.
**C. Decide from functional status.** Independence informs prognosis but cannot substitute for her priorities.
**D. Time with grandchildren.** Explore acceptable hospitalization risk and time away from home in concrete terms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1045.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 85-year-old man with mild dementia (MMSE 22), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45) has developed increasing difficulty managing finances, finding his way to familiar places, and taking medications over three weeks. His wife died six months ago. His daughter asks about supported accommodation, but he wants to remain at home. Examination and routine laboratory results are normal. Alongside evaluation of this recent change, which approach directly assesses whether his home setting can meet his current needs?
o: Use the dementia diagnosis to arrange placement before reviewing the home setting.
Use office cognitive testing to determine safety before reviewing the home setting.
Arrange home safety assessment and a trial of support matched to his needs.
Start donepezil and defer review of the home setting until a later visit.
explanation:
Safe community living depends on whether a person's actual deficits can be covered at home. The recent three-week change warrants medical evaluation while the team identifies specific risks in medication use, navigation and finances.

**Arrange a home safety assessment and trial of targeted support.** This tests whether his preference to remain at home can be met safely.

**A. Placement on diagnosis alone.** The diagnosis gives no information about the layout, routines, available supervision or tasks he can still perform.
**B. Office cognitive testing alone.** A test score cannot show whether he gets lost outside his home or takes the right tablets there.
**C. Home assessment and support.** Review each failing task, put assistance in place and reassess whether it works in practice.
**D. Donepezil before safety review.** A possible symptomatic treatment cannot make current medication errors or wandering safe while the family waits.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 118, 915–916.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: למטופלת בעלת יכולת לקבל החלטות מוצע טיפול נשימתי ב-BiPAP. היא חוששת מהמשמעות של טיפול זה. איזה מידע יש למסור לצורך הסכמה מדעת לפי סעיף 13 לחוק זכויות החולה?
